We're Working Hard to Make
Every Stay Memorable
My husband and I stayed 2 nights at Rifrafters while in the area to visit New River Gorge National Park. Upon arrival the staff was very welcoming and helpful. We were escorted to our site and guided as we backed in. We hiked along the path around the campground. We used the very reasonably priced laundry. We also found the showers to be above average with plenty of hot water. We would stay there again!
RV Thayer
We stayed 4 nights. Upon arrival the staff was very friendly and helpful. We were guided to our site and was assisted backing in the RV to the site. I had some trouble hooking up my sewer connection, the staff member assisted me and gave me some very helpful advice. The park was quiet and very well attended to. The showers and bathrooms were very clean. Hiking trails were not difficult at all.
johnb63
I booked a site about 3 months ago and when I arrived at the campground, i noticed my site didn’t have a sewage hookup. I only stayed one night, but didn’t want to have to use the dump station. I talked to office personnel and they gladly put me in a site with sewage. No fuss, they just did it. I am staying there again for one night on May 30 and they changed my site for me. The bathroom is clean and the wifi is very good. I definitely would recommend this campground to stay at.
Crow305
Bathrooms were very clean and heated. Campsite was clean and we had a great view. Construction was going on at a cabin two sites up and when I asked if they could cut the noise a little sooner so we could enjoy the quiet they were very amenable.
Rgood1120

Season & Office Hours
Regular Season – April 1st to November 1st

General
Reservations are recommended.
A two night minimum stay is required for the following:
Memorial Day weekend, 4th of July weekend, Labor Day weekend and Bridge Day (3rd weekend in October).
Discounts: Good Sam, Harvest Host and Military (active and veteran) – 10%
Click here to renew/signup for Good Sam.
For military, please provide id at check in.
Deposit
A deposit, equal to a one night stay, plus tax is required when making a reservation.
The balance is due at check in.
Online Booking
$7.00 non-refundable online booking fee
Site Lock
You may choose to lock your site for a $10.00 non-refundable fee, if you would like a specific site
or cabin. The lock fee would guarantee that specific site or cabin.
If you choose not to lock the site, the site type you choose (RV full hook up, RV water and electric, Cabin,
Primitive tent or Tent with water electric) will remain the same.
Cancellations
Call the office at 304-574-1065 to cancel your reservation.
We will accept a cancel request via the guest portal.
14 days prior to your arrival – The deposit will be refunded less a $15 cancellation fee
Less than 14 days prior to your arrival – No refund
The online booking fee and the lock fee are non-refundable
We can reschedule your reservation at no charge.
Refunds
Will not be given due to inclement weather or any other circumstance beyond our control.
If you leave early, for any reason, the amount you paid for your reservation will not be refunded.
No Shows
Will forfeit the deposit, all fees paid and their site. Your site will not be held.
Arrivals / Departures
Check out: 12 pm (noon) EST.
If a later check out is needed, call the office for approval.
Check in: anytime after 2 pm
EARLY arrivals will be charged a $10 fee for every hour before 2 pm. The fee is waived with prior approval from management before arrival. Call the office 304-574-1065 for approval.
No early arrivals before 1pm.
Late Night Arrivals
There will be a map with your name, site number and directions to get to your site on it, in a basket located near
the front door of the office.

Creekside Loop
Walk-to Tent Area
Walk-to Tent Area
Each Creekside campsite is complete with a picnic table, fire ring with grill setup. All Creekside sites are full hookups. The sites are situated directly along Tub Run in a quiet and serene setting. Sites range in length from 35-45 feet, allowing for a variety of campers and RVs. There is a two tent or one camper and one tent limit per site.
Walk-to Tent Area
Walk-to Tent Area
Walk-to Tent Area
Each Walk-to campsite is complete with a picnic table, fire ring with grill setup, and lantern holder pole. The sites are situated directly along Tub Run in a quiet and serene setting. The walking distance from the parking area to the sites is approximately 60 feet. Each site is approximately 580 square feet. Walk-to campsites can be also reserved for group camping. There is a two tent limit per site.
Lakeside Loop
Walk-to Tent Area
Lakeside Loop
Each Lakeside campsite is complete with a picnic table and fire ring with grill setup. The sites are situated directly on the Youghiogheny River Lake. The playground, swim beach, and dump station are all located on the Lakeside Loop. Sites range in length from 40-55 feet, allowing for a variety of campers and RVs. There is a two tent or one camper and one tent limit per site.

Reservation Information
Contact us by phone or email for personal attention to your reservation. We accept Visa, MasterCard or Discover for securing reservations by phone. Your credit card will not be charged, but deposits will be charged according to the Cancellation Policy listed below.
No refunds for early departure.
We reserve the right to substitute campsites.
Cancellation Policy
Standard Policy - A $10 cancellation fee applies to all cancellations. Cancellations must be made within 7 days or more of the scheduled arrival date or a 1 day camping fee will apply.
Holiday Policy - A $10 cancellation fee applies to all cancellations. Cancellations must be made within 10 days or more of the scheduled arrival date or a 1 day camping fee will apply.
Rate Information
Monthly and group rates are available. Please call the campground for more information.
All rates are based on one family unit per site per night. A family unit consists of 2 adults and 3 children under age 18. An extra charge of $5 per person per night for additional persons will apply. Maximum of 8 people per campsite.
Good Sam Discount applies only to Daily Rate.
Passport America® discount ~ some restrictions apply.
Check-In / Check-Out
Check-In - 2:00 p.m.
Check-Out - 1:00 p.m.
Pet Policy
Pets are welcome at Burnt Cabins Grist Mill & Family Campground FREE of charge.
Maximum number of pets allowed per campsite/RV site is 2.
Pets must be kept on a leash at all times.
No pet fencing permitted.
Be considerate - please always clean up after your pet!

Mercer County Fairgrounds, Inc. Camping Policy on Appearance of Camping Units
Purpose: The purpose of this policy is to maintain a clean, safe, and visually appealing environment at
the Mercer County Fairgrounds. This policy aims to ensure that all camping units present at the
fairgrounds meet a standard of appearance that reflects well on the community and the event.
Authority: This policy is enforced by the Mercer County Fair Board and the Executive Staff of the Mercer
County Fairgrounds, Inc. These authorized individuals have the discretion to dismiss from or not grant
camping privileges based on compliance with this policy.
Policy Guidelines:
1. General Appearance:
• All camping units must be kept clean, tidy, and in good repair.
• Camping units should not display any form of peeling paint, rust, or other extensive wear
and tear that might detract from the overall appearance of the fairgrounds.
• Signage or decorations that are offensive, excessively worn, or unsightly are prohibited.
• No tent camping will be allowed, unless camping with a rally.
2. Safety and Maintenance:
• Camping units must be fully operational and meet all safety standards applicable to
mobile or temporary living quarters.
• All utilities and extensions from the camping units, such as power cords and hoses, must
be organized and must not pose a trip hazard or any other risk to safety.
3. Surrounding Area:
• The area surrounding the camping unit must be kept clean and free of debris.
• Equipment, furniture, and other outdoor items must be kept to a reasonable quantity and
maintained in a neat and orderly fashion.
4. Inspections:
• The Fair Board or Executive Staff may conduct inspections of camping units with prior
notice to ensure compliance with this policy.
• Campers will be notified of any non-compliance issues and will be given a reasonable time
frame to address such issues.
5. Non-Compliance:
• Failure to comply with the appearance guidelines may result in the camper being asked to
leave or not being granted camping privileges at future events.
• Decisions made by the Fair Board or Executive Staff regarding non-compliance are final.
Appeals Process: Campers who have been denied privileges or dismissed based on non-compliance
with this policy may appeal the decision in writing to the Mercer County Fair Board within 30 days of the
decision. The appeal should clearly state the grounds for reconsideration and any relevant information or
evidence that supports the case for reinstatement of privileges.
Implementation: This policy is effective immediately and applies to all current and future reservations
and occupants of camping spaces at the Mercer County Fairgrounds, Inc. All campers, upon reservation,
will receive a copy of this policy and must acknowledge their understanding and agreement to adhere to
the policy.

On-site Camping
Camping has never been so fun!
With over 100 sites available for rent, the camping facilities at Greene County Expo Center are modern, safe and most importantly, clean!
Your event’s attendees can enjoy their camping experience to the full with plenty of entertainment for the kids, including a playground, basketball court and tennis court.
After they’ve enjoyed the day’s activities, they can wash off in our designated shower house before settling down in front of their own warm fire ring.

100 camping places

Picnic tables and benches available on request
1000 sq ft lots (20x50ft)
RVs and tents welcome
Pets welcome
Fires rings permitted - firewood is available for purchase
Camping FAQs
Camping for Dayton Hamvention®
The Greene County Expo Center handles the on-site camping for the Dayton Hamvention®
We are currently holding a waiting list for camping spots we ask that you please click here to fill out the form to be added to the waiting list. We will contact you from the list if we have any spots become available.
Where do I buy a camping permit?
You can apply for one here or get in touch with us here .
Are your sites pet friendly?
Yes, pets are welcome to stay with you, but they do need to be approved first. When booking in, make sure to let us know you’re planning on bringing them with you. All pets must have a record of vaccines from certified veterinarian prior to your arrival.
Am I able to have an open fire?
No. Open fires are not permitted, however fire rings are, in pre-approved rings and sites.
What forms of electric hook up do you provide?
30 and 50 amps.
Is tent camping permitted?
Yes!
Are shower and bathroom facilities provided?
Yes, we have a designated shower building and full bathroom facilities available.
Camping Guidelines
All trailers, campers, trucks, and/or other vehicles used for living purposes must be parked within designated camping areas only.
All pets/animals kept on premises must have prior approval.
All pets must have record of vaccines from certified veterinarian prior to arrival on grounds.
Persons using electricity must provide compatible plugs and cords. Hook-ups are subject to electrician’s inspection.
All premises around the camping units must be kept clean and sanitary. Trash to be placed in containers. No dumping of any holding tanks will be permitted unless otherwise authorized by Expo Staff personnel. No gray water may be leaking from trailer. No trailers, campers, trucks, or other vehicles may be washed on the grounds using water sources on the grounds.
Use of illegal drugs or abuse of alcohol may result in campers being asked to leave the property. No refunds of camping money will be permitted.
Abuse of the benches, picnic tables, and/or any other property belonging to the grounds may result in the person signing the rental agreement to be assessed an additional charge.

Our Accommodations
Looking for somewhere to stay in the Xenia area? Here are our favorite places to stay in Xenia. On-site camping may also be an option depending on the type of event and availability. Click here to learn more about camping accommodations.
Victoria's Bed & Breakfast in Xenia
A local treasure, Victoria's Bed and Breakfast was built in 1881 by John Allen, a Xenia banker and member of the Ohio House of Representatives. The house has four air-conditioned bedrooms to stay in. It is an Eastlake style Victorian mansion with high ceilings, original wood trim, 25 rooms, 30 chandeliers and 9 fireplace mantles. If you're traveling in a group, you can even rent the entire house to yourself.
Rooms start at $99 per night or you can rent the whole place for $350 per night.
Hampton Inn & Suites Xenia Dayton
Xenia's Hampton Inn is always a popular choice. Less than a mile from Lewis A Jackson Regional Airport, there's an indoor pool and 24-hour business center on-site, perfect for business and pleasure trips!
Start your day with a free hot breakfast including a wide array of morning favorites. Unwind in a spacious room or suite with modern décor, free WiFi, flat-screen TV with premium cable and work desk with ergonomic chair. Upgrade to a suite for more space and sitting area with sofa bed.

Atwood Lake Country Campground in Carrollton, OH
Tucked into the rolling hills of Carroll County, Atwood Lake Country Campground blends peaceful scenery with guest-friendly comforts—offering a perfect escape whether you are staying for a weekend or the full season. The park features a range of accommodations to suit every style, including spacious RV sites, tent areas, and cozy standard or deluxe cabins equipped with climate control, kitchenettes, and inviting front porches. Whether you prefer roughing it under the trees or relaxing in a bed, every option puts you just steps away from the beautiful lake and outdoor fun.
The campground keeps things lively and comfortable with a swimming pool, vibrant playgrounds, and a quiet fishing pond perfect for teaching little ones how to cast a line. Weekends bring the community together with themed events, crafts, and laid-back gatherings around the campfire. As a pet-friendly park, your furry companions are always welcome to join the adventure. The main office is open daily from 10 AM to 6 PM, ensuring a friendly, simple, and memorable getaway focused on rest, recreation, and quality time with the people who matter most.

Camping
NOTE: If needing information about camping during the fair, please see the Fair Camping section under the County Fair header.
​
Camping is open from April 1st to July 4th and July 24th to October 31, weather permitting.
​
To reserve a camping spot online, please click
here .
​
No Camping the week Before or During the Johnson County 4-H and Agricultural Fair
​
Daily Camping Rate: $30* per day - Water Electric and Full Hookup Available
*Plus applicable sales tax
​
Please send all payments to:
Attn: Johnson County Fairgrounds
250 Fairground Street
Franklin, IN 46131
​
Campground Procedures:
Please check in with groundskeeper in Fair Office upon arrival. If Fair Office is not open, please check in with Campgrounds Host in campgrounds.
Hang tag must be displayed at all times.
Waivers must be signed and rent must be paid in advance before the electric will be turned on.
Rent must be paid in advance for the length of the stay, or in advance on a weekly basis.
To check in by mail, waivers will need to be witnessed by a notary and mailed in advance along with payment. Electric will then be turned on prior to arrival.
Reservations are preferred but not required. For Reservations outside of fair week, please contact the Fair Office at 317-738-3247 or email campgrounds@jocofairin.com
​
Campground Policies:
Shower house is available on the grounds.
Please pick up all trash!
Respect other campsites. Do not walk to park on other lots.
Pets should be kept inside and on a leash if outside.
​
Failure to abide by these procedures and
policies
may result in loss of your camping privileges.

Boat and RV Winter Storage
Boat & RV Storage - Thursday, October 1, 2026 through Wednesday, March 31, 2027
Ne
ed a place t
o keep your boat or recreational vehicles this winter?
You can store them inside at the Johnson County Fairgrounds!
​
We utilize Magill and Fitzpatrick Halls as well as the Indoor Arena and Livestock Pavilion for inside storage between October and March each winter. Contact the Fairgrounds Caretaker for more information, contracts/payments and to schedule your vehicle in for storage:
317-738-3247.
​
Pricing:
Up to 20' ($275.00)
Over 20' ($275 plus $5.00 for each additional
ft.)
​
Beginning October 1: Boats and RVs will be parked Sunday, October 1 from 8am until 2pm. Following October 1, Boats and RVs will be parked Monday-Friday, between 8:00 am and 2pm, until facilities are full.
​
All antennas MUST be either folded down or removed. MAXIMUM HEIGHT of vehicles is 11 ft. 6 in. Have your fuel tanks empty/near empty during storage. Remove all Perishable items. Cover your boat.
​
***Please Note: All vehicles not removed by the end storage period shall be subject to a fee of $50.00 each additional day the vehicle remains on the fairgrounds either in storage or parked on the grounds.
​
All vehicles removed before end of storage period shall be subject to an additional fee of $50.00. If you want to remove your vehicle early, please note this at the time of storage. This allows us to place it in a space that is easily accessible.
​

Rates & Reservations
Admission, Rates, and Reservations
Rates are subject to change.*
RESERVATIONS
* Reservations shall be made from Monday to Thursday from 9:00AM to 6:00PM only.
Reservations will not be taken Friday thru Sunday .*
Reservation are not and cannot be made by e-mail.
Click here for online reservations
Check-in for camping is at 1 pm, and check-out is at noon. If nobody is on your site before your day of arrival, you may arrive as early as 10 am, though you must call ahead.
Reservations can be made by phone, or in person. Campers using a trailer, mobile home, RV, or popup need to have the model, color, and license plate information at hand.
Primitive Campsites are non-reservable. Check-in must be between 1:00PM and 9:00PM.
Electric Campsites and cabins must be paid in full for the duration of their stay when the reservation is made.
Maximum of 12 Nights in Modern Electric Sites, and 6 Nights in Primitive Sites
Sites cannot be reserved by a customer, for another customer, unless the transaction is paid in full at the time of reservation.
For private group rentals (Recreation Building, and Flory Shelter) $150 damage deposit must be paid to confirm the reservation; upon arrival, $150 must be paid along with the $5 gate fee for each attendee, unless other arrangements are made. If the area is found to be clean upon inspection after the event, the $150 damage deposit will be refunded to the customer.
The waterfall area is non-reservable.
If a customer does not show up by check-in on the second day of the reservation, it becomes forfeit, unless prior notice is given.
When making camping reservation this is the information will need to have. If you are making reservations for other campers, you will need to have their complete information.
Cancellations
Only the reservation holder can cancel or make changes to an existing reservation.
If a reservation is canceled 8 or more days before arrival, a flat $10 cancellation fee will be charged (per site that is canceled.)
If a reservation is canceled between 1 and 7 days before arrival, the first night's rental fee will be charged as a cancellation fee.
If a reservation is canceled on or after the day of arrival, the customer will forfeit their entire rental fee.
Reservation dates may be switched upon request; however, it is not guaranteed you will get the same site. (Does not apply on holiday weekends.)
No refunds will be given due to inclement weather
Note the $5 reservation fee is a separate fee and will not be included with your cancellation as it is a processing fee.
France Park Golf Cart Rules 2026
* Campers must register their golf carts at the campground office and display the provided sticker permit where visible by park staff.
* Drivers must be licensed and at least 16 years old. 12 to 16 years of age must have a responsible licensed adult next to them while operating golf cart.
* Golf carts are not to be driven by non-licensed person on holiday weekends. NO EXCEPTIONS!
* Golf carts must be operated responsibly and courteously. Drivers should avoid distractions, drive within speed limits, and may not operate under the influence.
* Golf carts must be maintained to prevent excessive noise and smoke.
* Engines must be same as stock. No motor larger than stock will be allowed.
* Golf carts must give pedestrians the right of way and follow all rules that pertains to a vehicle.
* Golf carts must have working lights and reflectors to be driven after dark. The driver must be licensed if operated after dark.
* You are only permitted to carry as many passengers as your seating will allow.
* Golf carts must not be operated in a way that disturbs others or the natural environment.
* Owners are responsible for any injuries or damage to park or private properties caused by their golf cart.
* Golf carts must be parked at camp site from 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. with the exception to use for transportation to and from restroom or the park office.
* Park staff reserves the right to revoke golf cart privileges to any camper at any time.
* France Park is not responsible for stolen or damaged golf carts or accidents, damages, injuries, and or deaths of any kind related to the use of a Golf Cart.
* France Park will not be towing anyone that is stuck or broke down in camping areas or on trails.
* Golf carts must be parked in proper designated areas. Golf carts are not authorized to park on beach, on areas going down to beach, or any other areas vehicles are not authorized to park.
* Golf carts are to remain on premade authorized roads and trails.
Season Passes
Season passes are from Jan.1 - Dec.31
Golf Cart Pass must be purchased, and proof of insurance is required. The pass and insurance are required for all golf carts. Proof of insurance can be mailed to the park. The cost is $25.00 and will be good for the calendar year and purchased annually.

Reserve | Scales Lake Park
LAST SWIMMING DAY WILL BE SUNDAY AUGUST 2, 2026.
BEACH WILL BE CLOSED FOR THE SEASON AFTER THIS DATE AND WILL REOPEN MAY 2027.
WINTER RESERVATIONS
WATER AT ALL CAMPSITES WILL BE TURNED OFF AFTER THE FIRST HARD FREEZE, AND WILL REMAIN OFF UNTIL SPRING OF THE FOLLOWING YEAR. PLEASE PLAN ACCORDINGLY WHEN RESERVING.
One responsible individual is required to register personally for his group or family with park staff for each site. This is required when making reservations both online and in person.
Please be aware that tents are not allowed on Full Hook Up sites.
For Water and Electric reservations, you may have one RV and one tent, or two tents.
Please note that the maximum stay for tent camping is three nights.

“Lovin’ Life at Sugar Creek Glen”
MAKE A RESERVATION
Welcome to Sugar Creek Glen Campground
Have you been searching for a unique camping experience in the Finger Lakes region? Somewhere to unwind, relax and spend quality time with your family and friends? Or maybe simply a place to enjoy the quiet and beauty of nature?
If so, we have what you’re looking for. Just five miles off I-390, Sugar Creek Glen Campground offers a small corner of paradise in Dansville, New York, including beautiful creekside scenery and five waterfalls located on privately owned campground property.
Please note: Sugar Creek Glen is a private campground. Access to the creek, glen, trails and waterfalls is exclusively for registered camping guests. We do not offer public hiking, day-use admission or separate waterfall access. Learn more on our Waterfall Access page .
Registered guests can enjoy many ways to spend their time while camping with us. Explore the glen and waterfalls during your stay, go trout fishing, participate in campground activities, gather around the campfire on a cool summer night, enjoy s’mores with family and friends, or simply slow down and enjoy the peaceful surroundings.
Come camp with us and discover the hidden jewel of New York’s Southern Tier at Sugar Creek Glen Campground, where memorable Finger Lakes camping experiences begin.
Your Hosts,
Merav & Daniel

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Is Sugar Creek Glen Campground open to the public for hiking?
No. Sugar Creek Glen Campground is private property. The creek, glen, trails and waterfalls are available only to registered camping guests. We do not offer public hiking access or day-use admission.
Who can access the creek and waterfalls?
Access is reserved for registered guests staying at Sugar Creek Glen Campground. Guests may enjoy the creek, glen and waterfalls as part of their camping experience. Learn more on our Waterfall Access page .
Do you offer day-use passes or separate waterfall admission?
No. Sugar Creek Glen Campground does not offer day-use passes, hiking admission or separate access to the waterfalls. Access is included with a registered camping stay.
Where is Sugar Creek Glen Campground located?
Sugar Creek Glen Campground is located at 11288 Poags Hole Road in Dansville, New York, in the Finger Lakes and Southern Tier region, just a few miles from I-390.
How do I make a camping reservation?
Camping reservations can be made through our online reservation system. Choose your dates, select an available campsite and complete your reservation online.

2027 Monthly RV Rate
Standard RV Site — $850 / 28-Day Stay
Monthly rates are calculated as a 4-week (28-day) stay.
Metered electric is additional.
One sewer pump-out service per week is included.
The monthly rate includes a family of up to 2 adults and 3 children.
Reservations
Check-In: 3:00pm – 8:00pm
Earlier check-in is possible between 1:00pm – 3:00pm if pre-arranged and is subject to an additional $25.00 charge. There are no check-ins prior to 1:00pm.
Check-Out:
Campsites — 1:00pm
Cabins — 11:00am
Later check-out, allowing guests to remain at Sugar Creek Glen Campground, may be arranged as follows:
Tent Sites: Site must be vacated and cleaned by 1:00pm. Vehicles must be moved to the guest parking area.
Cabins: Cabin must be vacated and cleaned by 11:00am. Vehicles must be moved to the guest parking area.
RV Sites: If the site is not reserved for another guest, the RV may remain on site.
In all cases, there is an additional $10.00 per hour charge . All late departures must end no later than 5:00pm.
2-night minimum on weekdays and weekends.
3-night minimum on holiday weekends.
Access to certain cabins and tent sites requires driving through Sugar Creek.
Full payment is required at the time of reservation.
Cancellations
Up to 10 days prior to your scheduled check-in date, you may cancel your reservation and receive a full refund, less a $25 cancellation fee. You may also change the dates of your stay if the request is made more than 10 days before your scheduled check-in date. Once a reservation has been changed, a cancellation is non-refundable. When 10 days or less remain before your scheduled arrival, the reservation is non-refundable and dates cannot be changed.
Holiday weekend reservations are non-refundable.
Your reservation is considered a “no show” if you have not arrived by 11:00am the day following your scheduled arrival and have not canceled the reservation or contacted the campground office to hold your site.
Payment for camping nights is non-refundable for no-show reservations.
Visitors
Day passes are no longer available for hiking “The Glen.” Waterfall and glen access is reserved for registered campers and their permitted guests.
Registered campers are allowed to have guests and visitors within the following guidelines:
Daily Guest Fee: $10.00 per person
Overnight Guest Fee: $15.00 per adult, dependent upon space availability on the campsite
Maximum of 4 visitors per campsite
Visiting hours are 9:00am – 10:00pm
All visitors must register at the office before entering the campground and must park their vehicles in the visitor parking area located at the campground entrance.
For more information about access to the campground’s private waterfalls and glen, please visit our Waterfall Access page .
Seasonal Camping
If you’re interested in spending the season at Sugar Creek Glen Campground, visit our Seasonal Camping page or call 585-335-6294 for more information.
Camping is an outdoor activity; therefore, refunds are not provided due to the discomforts of nature or premature departure.
Camping Rates FAQ
Have questions about rates, reservations, or what is included with your stay? Here are a few of the most common questions we receive.
What is included in the campsite rate?
Rates are based on one family unit per site and include up to two adults and their children under 18 years old. Site occupancy is limited to a maximum of five people.
Is there a minimum stay requirement?
Yes. Sugar Creek Glen Campground requires a two-night minimum on weekdays and weekends and a three-night minimum on holiday weekends.
Do you offer monthly RV site rates?
Yes. For 2027, the monthly rate for a Standard RV Site is $850 for a 4-week (28-day) stay, plus metered electric. The rate includes one sewer pump-out service per week and accommodates a family of up to 2 adults and 3 children.
Are additional guests allowed?
Yes. Registered campers may have visitors subject to campground visitor policies . Daily guests are $10 per person, and overnight adult guests are $15 per person when space is available on the campsite.
When is payment due for a reservation?
Full payment is required at the time the reservation is made.
Do you offer seasonal camping?
Yes. Seasonal camping is available at Sugar Creek Glen Campground. Visit our Seasonal Camping page or call 585-335-6294 for more information.

RV & Tent Camping Near Dansville, NY
Whether you’re traveling with your RV or prefer sleeping beneath the stars, Sugar Creek Glen Campground offers camping options surrounded by the natural beauty of the Finger Lakes region. Choose the site that fits your camping style and enjoy a relaxing getaway near Dansville, New York.
Comfortable RV Camping
RV Camping Sites
Enjoy the convenience of water and electric hookups while camping in a peaceful, wooded setting. Our RV sites provide the essentials for a comfortable stay, with helpful campground services available when you need them.
Water and 30-amp electric hookups at all RV sites
Limited sites with 50-amp electric service
Picnic table and fire ring at every site
Maximum camper length of 38 feet, with individual site-length limits
Dump station available at checkout at no additional charge
Honey wagon service available for an additional fee through the office
Important: RV sites have water and electric hookups. Sewer service is handled through the campground’s dump station or optional honey wagon service. Please select a site that accommodates your camper’s length.
Check-in: 3:00–8:00 PM
Check-out: 1:00 PM
RESERVE AN RV SITE →
Get Closer to Nature
Tent Camping Sites
Experience traditional tent camping at Sugar Creek Glen. From rustic sites to sites with electricity, and from waterfront locations to more secluded settings, there are options for different camping preferences.
Rustic and electric tent camping options
Waterfront and secluded sites available
Picnic table and fire ring at every site
Access to tent sites by driving across the creek
Camping vehicles are not permitted on tent sites
Check-in: 3:00–8:00 PM
Check-out: 1:00 PM

Good to Know Before You Go
Camping Sites Frequently Asked Questions
Do RV sites have full hookups?
RV sites offer water and electric hookups, with 30-amp service at all RV sites and limited 50-amp availability. A dump station is available at checkout at no additional charge, and honey wagon service can be arranged for an additional fee.
What is the maximum RV length?
The campground can accommodate campers up to 38 feet long. Individual sites have specific length limits, so be sure to select a site appropriate for your RV when booking.
Are electric tent sites available?
Yes. Sugar Creek Glen offers both rustic and electric tent camping options, including waterfront and more secluded sites.
Can I bring a camping vehicle onto a tent site?
No. Camping vehicles are not permitted on the campground’s tent sites. Tent-site access involves driving across the creek.
What are the check-in and checkout times?
Check-in is from 3:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and checkout is at 1:00 PM for both RV and tent camping sites.
Do campsites include picnic tables and fire rings?
Yes. Every RV and tent campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring for guests to enjoy during their stay.

Use this campsite map to explore the layout of Sugar Creek Glen Campground in the Finger Lakes region of New York. The map shows the location of RV sites, tent sites, cabins, RV rental, seasonal sites, trails, Sugar Creek, and key campground amenities to help you choose the right spot for your stay.
Find the Right Site at Sugar Creek Glen
This map gives you a clear picture of how Sugar Creek Glen Campground is laid out, from wooded camping loops to open areas near amenities. Whether you’re traveling with an RV, pitching a tent, or staying in a cabin, the map helps you understand where each site type is located within the campground.
Map Key – What the Numbers & Icons Mean
RV Sites are marked by yellow site numbers
Seasonal Sites are marked by black site numbers
Rustic Tent Sites are marked by orange site numbers
Electric Tent Sites are marked by red site numbers
Cabins, potable water, pavilion, dump station, rec hall, playground, store/office, dumpsters, visitor parking, and trails are shown with icons on the map
Tips for Choosing a Campsite
If you prefer to be close to campground amenities, choose sites near the store, rec hall, playground, and pavilion.
For a quieter stay, look for sites farther from main activity areas and closer to the wooded sections of the park.
Guests who enjoy walking and exploring may want a site near the Glen Trail or Woods Trail for easy access to scenic paths.

Conveniently located on East 17th Street in Trenton, Lantern Lights RV Park offers a comfortable place to stay in the rolling countryside of northern Missouri. Grocery stores, restaurants, fuel, and local services are just a short drive away, with a nearby walking trail for getting out and stretching your legs.
Our back-in RV sites include full hookups, and our grounds are kept clean and tidy. Families, solo travelers, and pets are welcome.
Lantern Lights RV Park does not have showers, bathrooms, or laundry facilities available on-site. Please plan accordingly.
We're open year-round and welcome overnight, weekly, and extended stays. Whether you're passing through, working in the area, or planning a longer visit to Trenton, we'd be happy to have you.

FAIR CAMPERS, CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFOMATION
Campgrounds 1715 10th St. Boone, IA 50036
The Boone County Fairgrounds offers a modern, clean, and well-maintained campgrounds located east of the fairgrounds.
Campgrounds open year round!
Full hookup campsites have water/sewer connections on year round (even during the cold winter months)! Winter camping is allowed for self-contained trailers who are prepared for winter camping. Contact the office for more details on winter time camping.
Bathroom/Shower House is open April 1 - November 1 (unless unusually cold temperatures occur)
Location
The Campgrounds is close to everything in Boone and only 15 minutes away from Ames and Iowa State University. We are also conveniently located within 40 minutes of the Des Moines metro area. Local attractions in Boone include Ledges State Park, the Boone Racetrack, Boone and Scenic Valley Railroad, and many other attractions.
Facilities
- Nearly 100 Camp Sites
- Shower House
- Flushing Toilets
- Electrical Service: 20, 30 or 50 Amp Hookups
- Water Hookups (not at every campsite)
-Sewer Hookups (not at every campsite)
- Dump Station
- Pens for horses available for $25/horse/night (please contact the office for making reservations for this).
Stay Limits
- There is a 14 day stay limit on sites 1-76 & 87-96
- If you wish to stay more than 14 days, you must contact the Fair
Office to make arrangements. Long term campers must camp in
sites 77-86. (Long term discounts available, call for details)
Registration and Reservations
Pre-registration can only be done online.
If you do not pre-register online, you can camp at a walk up registration site. Campers who do not pre-register must complete a registration form and submit payment in the drop-box located at the Shower House.
- All payment is due in advance.
- Online reservations collect card payment with reservations.
- Walk up registrations must register and pay upon arrival, before setting up your campsite.
Rates
Primitive Camping (no hookups)
$10/night
Electric Only (we have 20, 30 or 50 amps available)

$100/week (7 nights)
$325/month (30 or 31 nights)

Fees include use of shower and bathroom facilities and dump station usage.
Cost for using the dump station if you are not camping with us is $10. Please call ahead at 515-432-5899, as our dump station is locked at all times.
Cost for showering on site, of you are not camping with us is $5/person

BOONE COUNTY FAIRGROUNDS CAMPGROUNDS RULES
General Terms
Processing fee is required for all reservations.
The person registered will be responsible for the condition of the campsite.
Reservations are not refundable for any reason .
We reserve the right to not renew a booking to any guest who has not arranged for all of their dates in advance. We will do our best to move guests to the next best available site (if necessary).
Rates are only guaranteed at the time of booking and are subject to change at any time without notice. Changes made to your reservation after it has been confirmed may result in higher rates. Required Deposits 100% of your total stay is due at the time of booking.
Check-In and Check-Out Check-in between 1pm & 10pm. Check out by 11am.
Cancellation Policy
Online Reservation are paid 100% at the time of booking. No refunds.
No Show policy- Guests failing to cancel their reservation within the required time will be considered a no show and subject to the same cancellation policy as listed above.
Walk up only sites may be occupied for a maximum of 14 days and fees should be deposited in the box no less than a daily basis. General Guidelines
Quiet hours are from 10pm to 8am.
The number of camping units per site is one camper and one tent with no more than two vehicles. This includes the tow vehicle. Guests should park additional vehicles in the field south of the campground.
All garbage and litter must be deposited in the dumpster and not in fire pits. Please bag all garbage.
Campsites should be clean and neat, free of fire hazards and clutter.
Customers shall not make any alteration to the electric, water or sewer connections at the campground.
Customers should adhere to specific legal requirements when connecting to sewer, water and electric services at the campground/resort.
No extra air conditioners, wires, hoses, or cords running except through the OEM port.
Report issues with utilities at your campsite to the camp host or fair office.
Sanitary dumps are available at designated areas for registered camper usage only.
All alleys and drives throughout the campground must be clear and accessible to traffic and EMS vehicles.
Speed Limit in the Camping area is 5 MPH.
Biking is not allowed in the campgrounds after dark.
Campfires are permitted in designated fire rings (please do not move fire rings) If you campsite does not have a fire ring, you may have an above ground fire ring.
Campers must camp only in those places specifically provided or marked.
Quads that are not registered for the road may not be used on the grounds. This includes dirt bikes. Golf carts are acceptable only within the campground.
Alcoholic beverages are permitted in the campground only, but intoxication will not be tolerated.
Be respectful of occupied sites.
No smoking in the restrooms.
We are not responsible in case of the theft of a camper/tent or contents thereof.
We are not responsible for any damage caused by natural causes nor spoilage of food caused by power outages.
Management reserves the right to call law enforcement and ask for immediate removal of campers. No refunds will be offered. Pets
Pets are welcome in the campground but should be kept on leashes (six-foot maximum length or inside the camper).
Pets may not be left unattended at a campsite.
Pets are not allowed in the campground restroom or in the gated area of the fairgrounds.
Bring waste bags to pick up after your pet.
Excessive barking will not be tolerated.
No dangerous, aggressive or poisonous pets of any kind are permitted.
Management reserves the right to reject any pet.
Pets shall be up to date on rabies vaccinations id tag with owner’s phone number attached to the collar.
Pet owners must clean up after their pets.
Pets should not be an annoyance, or a danger to the other occupants or visitors of the campground.
The campground shall have no liability to family members or guests for any damage or injury to persons or property caused by any pet. Prohibited Activities
No illegal, or offensive activities shall be conducted at any site, nor shall anything be done within the campground which is or could become an unreasonable annoyance or nuisance to neighboring sites.
Firearms and Fireworks are prohibited in the campground.
We will not tolerate abusive or disruptive behavior whether directed at management or other persons.
Smoking is not permitted in any of our buildings, including restrooms. Smoking material must be extinguished in an appropriate fire container.
Disorderly Persons, The following are grounds for reservation termination and removal from the property: loud noise, whether mechanical, musical or vocal, use of foul or indecent language, causing damage to property of the campground or another person, drunken disorderly conduct, failing to follow rules, failing to follow directions of the property staff, threatening or abusive behavior or any other conduct that is not the type of behavior that is expected at a family campground.
No camper or vehicle repairs/remodeling in the campgrounds. Damage
Customers are responsible for all damage or destruction of property, and any injury to persons, caused by the guest or his or her family, visitor or pets. We reserve the right to charge guests accordingly for any damage they cause to the grounds and/or campground/resort facilities, including but not limited to broken waterlines, damaged/missing sewer connections, cable lines, landscaping, and excessive debris (bottle caps, zip ties, cigarette butts, etc.). Cold Weather Camping
By October 15th all campers must be approved by winter stay
Must be a fully winterized camper (heated pipes, etc.)
Must have a working toilet (as the bathroom and shower house will be closed)
Camper is responsible for ensuring hookups to the hydrant are insulated. If they hydrant freezes, you will be responsible to pay for replacing it. Minimum Age Requirements
By accepting a reservation, you acknowledge and agree to these rules and that: you are 18+ years of age and personally staying on the campsite that has been reserved.

About Us
Hiles-Pine Lake Campground is located at 8896 W. Pine Lake Road in Hiles, Wisconsin. Our season is from
May 1st through October 1st.
We offer primitive tent sites, 20 amp tent sites without water, 30/20 amp sites with water, and 50/30 amp sites with water. We currently do not have any sites with septic.
We also have a 30-foot camper rental and two
336 square-foot cabins available.
Check-In is at 3:00 pm. Check-Out is at 11 am.
The campground has 454 feet of shoreline on Pine Lake, a 1,673 acre lake located in Forest County. The lake offers Panfish, Largemouth Bass, Smallmouth Bass, Northern Pike and Walleye.
The Department of Natural Resources stresses the importance of buying wood where you plan on burning it to avoid the spread of invasive species.
Since Hiles-Pine Lake Campground is connected to the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, we ask that you do not bring in outside wood. We have wood for sale in the campground.
Nearby local attractions include Crandon International Raceway (13 miles), Mole Lake Casino (17 miles), Potawatomi Carter Casino (38 miles), over 300 miles of Public ATV trails, hiking trails, over 17,000 acres of lakes, rivers and streams to explore, museums, water shows, festivals and dozens of exceptional dining establishments.
The Swimming Pond & Beach
We have the perfect spot for you to relax. The swimming pond and beach area is a great addition to the campground.
We offer daily Adult, Child and Family passes for our guests.
Camp Store
Forget to pack some essentials? No worries, we have you covered. Check out our Camp Store for beverages, paper products, coffee supplies, canned foods, medicine and RV supplies.
We also have souvenirs, specialty soaps, dog products and T-shirts.
Primitive Sites
For campers looking for a more natural setting, we offer primitive sites. These sites do not have electric or water.
The primitive area in the lower meadows makes a great place for group camping.
20 Amp Tent or RV Sites
Our 20 amp sites are great for tents or RVs that don't need a 30/50 amp site. Water is not included on the site but is located nearby at the shower house.
The 20 amp site area is also great for group camping.
30 Amp Sites
We offer back-in sites with 30 amp and water.
There are 30 amp sites on the lakefront and throughout the campground.
50 Amp Sites - Pull Thru
We offer pull-thru sites with 50 amp and water.
There are pull-thru 50 amp sites on the lakefront and near Pine Lake Road.
50 Amp Sites - Back-in
We offer back-in sites with 50 amp and water.
There are 50 amp sites on the lakefront and throughout the campground.
Camper Rental
Our 30-foot camper rental sleeps up to six people. There is a queen bed, queen sleeper sofa and pull-down futon.
The camper has a fully-equipped kitchen with fridge, microwave, stove/oven and kitchen sink. The dining table seats four people.
The camper has a toilet and sink but no shower. The shower house is across the road for your convenience.
The camper has air conditioning and heat.
Kitchen necessities are included along with bedding and towels.
No pets or smoking allowed in the camper.
Cabin Rental
We have two 336 square foot cabin rentals that sleep up to six people. There is a queen bed, queen sleeper sofa and bunk beds.
The cabin has a fully-equipped kitchen with fridge, microwave, cooktop and kitchen sink. The dining table seats four people.
The cabin does not have a bathroom but the shower house is located nearby.
The cabin has an AC/Heat unit.
Kitchen necessities are included along with bedding and towels.
No pets or smoking allowed in the cabin.
Guest Boat Slip with Fishing Pier
Plan your camping trip and bring your boat!
Our boat launch gives you direct access to Pine Lake. Then dock your boat on the guest pier for an additional $8.00 per night. Reservations are required.
Fishing at Hiles-Pine Lake Campground
The campground has 454 feet of shoreline on Pine Lake, a 1,673 acre lake located in Forest County. The lake offers Panfish, Largemouth Bass, Smallmouth Bass, Northern Pike and Walleye.
We have a fish-cleaning house for your convenience!
DISCOUNTS
Active Military, Veterans & First Responders receive 10% discount off Reservations. Discount is applied at check-in. Identification is required.

Thurston Park
Thurston Park Campground, Central Lake
A family campground in the heart of Antrim County’s Chain of Lakes.
Welcome to Thurston Park, Central Lake’s premier park and a beloved family campground nestled in the heart of Antrim County’s Chain of Lakes. With its prime location at the northwest end of Intermediate Lake, Thurston Park offers an exceptional outdoor experience for both tent campers and RV enthusiasts.
At Thurston Park, we take pride in providing excellent facilities and amenities to enhance your stay. Whether you’re looking to embark on a boating adventure, relax on the beach, or engage in family-friendly activities, our park has something for everyone. Every campsite is furnished with a fire ring, and a picnic table for you to enjoy.
Camping Reservation Portal Opening
Our reservation portal will open the 2nd Tuesday of January of the corresponding year at 8am.
Example: The 2026 season Camping Reservation Portal will open on January 13, 2026 at 8am, as it is the 2nd Tuesday in January of 2026.
Our camping season spans from the first Friday in May to the first Sunday in October.
Thurston Park Campground
7854 Bradford Street
Central Lake, Michigan
49622
Thurston Park Campground Rules
Thurston Park Campground Guide
Seasonal/ Annual Camper Policy
Seasonal/ Annual Camper Contract
Call for additional information at:
231-676-8539- Camp Host: Char & Ron Snay
They live on property and are available 7 days a week during season.
231-544-6483- Village Office:
Available Monday- Thursday 7:15am-4:15pm.
We now accept online reservations and you can pay with Visa, MasterCard or Discover!
Departure Time Policy Change:
Campers will now need to vacate the property at 12:00pm, noon, on their departure date. This policy has been enacted for the 2025 camping season and into the future.
Sorry for any inconvenience.
For those eager to explore the sparkling waters, we offer a convenient boat launch, allowing you to set sail and discover the wonders of the Chain of Lakes. You’ll find limited waterfront campsites that provide a tranquil setting and the opportunity to wake up to stunning lake views.
Additionally, we offer limited full hook-up sites, ensuring your RV camping experience is comfortable and convenient. All sites are equipped with electric hook-ups to accommodate your needs. A dump station is also available for your convenience.
Our dedication to your comfort extends beyond camping amenities. Thurston Park features well-maintained restrooms and showers to ensure you can freshen up after a day of outdoor fun. A children’s playground offers a safe and enjoyable space for little ones to expend their energy, while children activities cater to the entire family’s entertainment.
We understand that pets are cherished members of the family, which is why Thurston Park welcomes dogs and other pets. You can bring your furry friends along to enjoy the great outdoors and create lasting memories together.
The park is designed to provide ample opportunities for relaxation and community gathering. Public docks are available for those who wish to take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront or cast a line into the crystal-clear lake. A charming gazebo offers a serene spot to take in the scenic beauty that surrounds you. Additionally, our pavilions are available for rent, making them ideal for hosting gatherings, picnics, or special events.
Thurston Park also caters to the modern needs of our guests. Stay connected with loved ones or share your outdoor experiences with the world, as we offer free WiFi throughout the park.
.
Thurston Park Campground
Whether you’re seeking a weekend getaway, a family vacation, or a peaceful retreat, Thurston Park is the perfect destination for you.
We invite you to immerse yourself in the beauty of Antrim County’s Chain of Lakes and experience the warmth and hospitality that define our premier park.
Our camping season spans from the first Friday in May to the first Sunday in October.

North Beach Campground
North Beach Campground
Nestled on the shores of beautiful Lake Champlain, in almost 45 acres of woods and beach, lies one of Burlington's hidden treasures - North Beach Campground.
There are 137 great sites to either pitch your tent or park your RV or trailer. With its premier municipal natural sand beach, shaded campsites and picnic grounds, North Beach offers an incomparable camping experience for any individuals wishing to camp in Vermont.
The campground is open May 15 through October 15.
Find out more about amenities at North Beach and the events happening in our parks .
View a map of North Beach Campground (PNG) .
Book Your Stay
All campground reservations must be made online .
2026 Online Reservation Opening Dates:
December 1, 2025 10am EST for Reservation dates: May 15, 2026 – June 28, 2026
January 5, 2026 10am EST for Reservation dates: June 29, 2026 – July 30, 2026
February 2, 2026 10am EST for Reservation dates: July 31, 2026 – September 7, 2026
March 4, 2026 10am EST for Reservation dates: September 8, 2026 – October 14, 2026
Book your stay!
For the first time ever we are offering longer-term campsites. Five full-hookup sites have been set aside for month-long stays. Those stays can be extended each month until the end of the season (May 15 - Oct. 15). A 50% deposit per month is needed to book these sites.
These sites cannot be booked online and must be done with the North Beach office through phone or email. If you are interested in booking a long-term campsite, please reach out to: nbcampground@burlingtonvt.gov
Contact
If you have any questions, please call the Campground Office at 802-862-0942 or email the North Beach Campground .
Security Phone Number: 802-316-6613
Rates & Amenities
Rates for May 15 through October 15:
Full Hook-up Site: $60
Water and Electric: $54
Tent Sites: $45
Lean-to: $50
Group sites: $100
Amenities
69 tent sites
29 full hookup RV sites
39 water and electric hookup trailer sites
Bathroom and hot shower facilities
Spacious activity areas and children's playground at beach
Picnic tables and campfires at all sites
Expansive, sunny beach
Picnic areas feature grills and tables
Direct access to 9 miles of bike path
Snack shack on the beach
Pets welcome, but must always be attended
Firewood available for purchase
Ice available for purchase at the snack shack from Memorial Day to Labor Day
Free Wi-Fi is made available by Burlington Telecom
Rules & Regulations
Welcome to Burlington's North Beach Campground. On our sandy beach you will find a snack bar, picnic tables, playground, pavilion, and entrances to our bike path. To ensure that all campers have a safe, satisfying, and pleasant camping experience we have a list of rules that must be followed.
Have fun.
Minimum age to rent a campsite is 18 years old.
Occupancy of a campsite shall not exceed 14 days after which you will be required to leave the campground for a minimum of 7 days before you can camp again.
The maximum number of adult occupants is as follows: 4 adults per tent site, 6 adults per water and electric site, and 8 adults per full hookup site. Note: we do not count kids in these numbers.
One person from the camping party must register with the campground office before entering the campground. When registering you must have the number of people staying on your site, camper's license plate number, vehicle license plate number, and your registration number.
The campsite must be occupied within 24 hours of the reservation date or the reservation will be forfeit.
Each site is allowed a maximum of 1 vehicle. Any visitors should register their vehicles and park in designated overflow parking areas.
There can be two camping units per site. Examples: on a water and electric site you can have a camper and a tent. On a tent site, you can have the tent you booked with the site and an extra tent. The cost for an extra tent is $5 per night.
Registered campers should show their camping passes at the gate when re-entering the campground on foot or in a vehicle.
Visitors will not be permitted after 2200 (10 pm). The beach will close at 2100 (9 pm) every night.
Children under the age of 8 years old must be accompanied by an adult when using the restroom and shower facilities.
It is the responsibility of the camper to keep their site neat and clean. All recycling and garbage must be put into the proper containers. Washing dishes is prohibited in the restroom sinks.
Pets are welcome, but must be under the control of the owner at all times. At no time should the pets be left alone on campsites. Pets must be kept on a 6-foot leash. Owners must clean up after their own pets.
Campground quiet hours are 22 (10 pm) until 7 (am).
Open consumption of alcohol is prohibited after 0000 (midnight), per city ordinance.
Check-in time is 1400 (2 pm). If your site is empty and has been cleaned then you are welcome to check in early. Check-out time is 1200 (noon). If you want to stay later and your site has no incoming reservations then you may extend until 1800 (6 pm) for a price of $15.
No items may be affixed or attached to trees within the park.
You are not allowed to bring wood onto the property; if you do it will be confiscated and destroyed. The reason for this is to keep invasive species from destroying our city trees. Wood and ice may be purchased at the campground office.
All rules and regulations are enforced by Waterfront Security and The Burlington Police Department.
Campground reservations are issued as defined in the Code of Ordinances of the City of Burlington Parks and Recreation Department, Appendix D, Section I(E), (6) and (7).
Cancellation Policy
If you cancel more than a week before your reservation, the fee is $10 plus the transaction fees. Failure to contact us or show up for your reserved date will result in forfeiture of the entire stay without refund.

Enjoy all that Burlington has to offer.

Get some lunch at the Kona Beachside restaurant down at our beach.

Campground Sites and Beach
Camper Sites
Our spacious camper sites are set in a picturesque field overlooking a scenic river, offering beautiful views and a peaceful atmosphere. Each site includes a water hookup, 30-amp and 50-amp electrical service, a picnic table, and a fire ring. With a minimum of 35 feet between sites, you'll enjoy plenty of space for your awning, outdoor seating, and relaxing in comfort.
We have a new bathhouse
New Sites All with Electric, Water, and Septic
We have Seasonal Sites Available for the 2027 Season
Call (603) 856-3101 for more information
Tent Sites
Our tent sites are nestled along the scenic river, offering a peaceful setting to relax and enjoy nature. Each site includes a picnic table and a fire ring, making it easy to enjoy meals outdoors and evenings around the campfire. For your convenience, a centrally located water spigot is available to all tent campers.
The Upper Ammonoosuc River
Bring your canoe or kayak and experience the peace and beauty of the Upper Ammonoosuc River as it gently flows alongside our campground. Whether you're looking for a relaxing paddle or a chance to enjoy nature, the river offers the perfect escape.
For hiking enthusiasts, the renowned Cohos Trail is located just 1.25 miles away, providing easy access to miles of scenic North Country adventure.
Private Trails
Explore nearly a mile of private trails winding throughout our property. These easy-to-enjoy trails are perfect for a relaxing walk or for young riders who are just learning to operate an ATV in a comfortable setting.
Looking for a little more excitement? We've also added a dedicated mud pit where ATV and UTV enthusiasts can splash, play, and get as muddy as they like before heading back to camp.

About The Lakes
Hardee Lakes Park is approximately 1200 acres and has horse trails, hiking trails, handicap-accessible hiking trails, and bike trails. There are 3 restrooms located throughout the park. The restrooms in the camping areas also have shower facilities available.
There are also picnic areas, a picnic pavilion, and a playground
available
. The park includes a boardwalk that winds around the lakes and through the woods, with an observation tower where people can watch wildlife.
The fisheries are controlled by the Florida Game and Fish Commission, and fishing is allowed in all the lakes. Hardee Lakes Park contains 4 lakes
in total
; Lake Hardee is 120 acres, Deer Lake is 110 acres, Lake Firefly is 97 acres, and Gator Lake is 47 acres.
Before you arrive at Hardee Lakes Park, please review the
Hardee Lakes Golf Cart UTV Policy
, Rules, and Regulations of Hardee Lakes, or a brochure that contains the fishing regulations and a summary of the park rules.
Real-Time Weather Data
To view real-time weather at Hardee Lakes, visit weatherstem.com .

Hardee Lakes
Nestled within 1,200 acres of woods and lakes, camping at Hardee Lakes offers a peaceful retreat with hiking trails, horseback paths, and a scenic boardwalk winding through the forest and wetlands. You can fish across four lakes, enjoy picnic areas and a pavilion, and stay comfortably overnight with restrooms and showers right in the camping zones. For more information about Hardee Lakes, visit the Hardee Lakes page .
Make a Camping Reservation
Pioneer Park
Camping at Pioneer Park offers 65 scenic campsites, including options both with and without water and electric hookups. You’ll have access to restrooms and showers, a convenient dump station, river and lake fishing, and quiet evenings ideal for relaxing by the campfire (with quiet hours from 10 PM to 8 AM). For more information about Pioneer Park, visit the Pioneer Park page .

The Probation and Community Services Department has been in existence since August 1977. The purpose of this department is to monitor and supervise court defendants placed on misdemeanor probation and community service in Hardee County. Work is performed under the Director of General Services.
Mission Statement
The mission of the Probation and Community Services Department is to provide supervision services to the court system for misdemeanor cases in Hardee County. These services are provided in such a manner as to ensure compliance with court-ordered obligations. Services are provided to ensure probationers’ assistance in living a worthwhile lifestyle, thereby being able to stay in society and contribute without putting extra burdens on the jail and welfare system.

Reservations
To make a reservation for camping at Pioneer Park, please use the site FireFly .
Real-Time Weather Data
To view real time weather at Pioneer Park visit http://hardee.weatherstem.com/fswnzolfosprings
Park Rules
To make your visit more enjoyable, please review the following Park guidelines. Pioneer Park is owned and administered by the County Government. Therefore, all camping units must have a current tag that is readily accessible to management.
Campsites Rules:
No alcoholic beverages are permitted on park premises.
1. Camp in designated sites
only.
2.Campsites are not a residence.
3.No mail or packages will be accepted for campers.
4.One camping unit & two vehicles per campsite. Camping unit and/or RV must be kept clean and in a good state of repair, which includes:
5.Clean; free of dirt, mold, and mildew.
6.Tarps will only be allowed for 14 days during construction/repair.
7. All campers/RVs entering Pioneer Park must be in good condition. All body work must be clean and in good repair. The camper/RV must be free from damage, rust, mold, and dirt.
8.All awnings and equipment must be well-maintained without any visible damage.
9.No ropes or wires shall be attached to trees or buildings.
10.The doormat shall be no larger than 3’ x4’.
11.All trash must be placed in garbage cans or dumpsters provided.
12.The dump station is located at the west end of the park. ($5.00 fee for non-campers).
13.No water is allowed to be dumped on the ground.
14.(washing of vehicles, trailers, or motor homes is prohibited)
15. No boards, pallets, blocks, or other such items on the grass.
16. All items outside of the site will be arranged in a neat and orderly fashion.
17.Campfires are allowed, but please be careful.
18.Campsites must be left clean & neat upon departure.
19.Restrooms with showers are available to registered campers. Showers are available to non-campers for a $5.00 fee per shower to be paid at the Park Office.
20.Children are always the responsibility of the parent/guardian.
21.Pets (two per campsite) are welcome but must be on a leash (not to exceed ten feet), and the owner is responsible for cleaning up all pet waste at the campsite and throughout the park. Pets are not permitted in any of the buildings or near the Wildlife Refuge area. Pet disturbance will not be tolerated at any time. Do not leave your pets unattended.
22. No swimming in any waters of the park.
23.Fishing is allowed from the banks of Pioneer Lake, Rock Lake, & Peace River. Boats are allowed on the Peace River only. The boat ramp is available.
24.Quiet time in the park is between 10:00 pm until 8:00 am. Please be respectful of other campers.
25.Park management reserves the right to ask any camper to vacate the park premises at any time, for any reason, including but not limited to violations of park rules, disruptive behavior, safety concerns, or any actions that may negatively impact the experience or well-being of other guests.

Hardee Lakes
Nestled within 1,200 acres of woods and lakes, camping at Hardee Lakes offers a peaceful retreat with hiking trails, horseback paths, and a scenic boardwalk winding through the forest and wetlands. You can fish across four lakes, enjoy picnic areas and a pavilion, and stay comfortably overnight with restrooms and showers right in the camping zones. For more information about Hardee Lakes, visit the Hardee Lakes page .
Make a Camping Reservation
Pioneer Park
Camping at Pioneer Park offers 65 scenic campsites, including options both with and without water and electric hookups. You’ll have access to restrooms and showers, a convenient dump station, river and lake fishing, and quiet evenings ideal for relaxing by the campfire (with quiet hours from 10 PM to 8 AM). For more information about Pioneer Park, visit the Pioneer Park page .

The Probation and Community Services Department has been in existence since August 1977. The purpose of this department is to monitor and supervise court defendants placed on misdemeanor probation and community service in Hardee County. Work is performed under the Director of General Services.
Mission Statement
The mission of the Probation and Community Services Department is to provide supervision services to the court system for misdemeanor cases in Hardee County. These services are provided in such a manner as to ensure compliance with court-ordered obligations. Services are provided to ensure probationers’ assistance in living a worthwhile lifestyle, thereby being able to stay in society and contribute without putting extra burdens on the jail and welfare system.

Trails
Located right on the Peace River, Brownville Park offers a convenient boat ramp to launch your kayak, canoe, or boat. Many kayakers and canoeists paddle north, up the picturesque Peace River, then turn around for a lazy and tranquil float back.
Day visitors ($2 fee) can explore this beautiful 75-acre park. A simple loop nature trail, perfect for small children, can be found on the south side of the park. On the north side are more extensive trails ideal for exploration.
Two trails at this 75-acre park lead you through floodplain forest and hardwood hammocks along the Peace River. The short, 0.25-mile nature trail in the southwest corner of the park begins at the campground; walk south along the river and an idyllic, cypress-lined stream in search of songbirds, dragonflies and butterflies.
Many visitors fish from the river banks and countless guests arrive with their families ready to picnic. Brownville Park offers recreational opportunities in a gorgeous natural setting with a family ambiance.
You can bring your camp gear and spend the night at one of our campsites . Nestled beneath the antique oak are campsites, both electric and non-electric.
A dump station is available for RV guests. The nearby restrooms include shower facilities for overnight camping guests.
Park Closes at Sundown. Sunday hours are from 12-Noon to Sunset.
Fees
Daily $2
Annual Pass $25
There is a $2 fee for daily visitors (campers are exempt). For more information on a $25 annual pass, contact Brownville Park at 863-491-5333 or the Parks and Recreation Office at 863-491-7507. Passes can also be purchased at Brownville Park with the Park Caretaker. The money collected will be used towards future improvements at the Park.

Please be aware that low river levels do not constitute any justification to avoid cancellation fees for camping reservations. We are happy to re-schedule reservations as needed if done prior to the 48 hour deadline.

Feature Overview
Feature Overview
Find a Facility
You can find facilities in a number of different ways. You may utilize our search functionality located on the left side of the screen. You can search through all facilities and look for specific features or search through reservable facilities during the specific time of your event. Feel free to put in as much or as little information to meet your need.
View facilities on the map to quickly see their general locations, or you can view information on the listing screen and sort them in a way that best meets your need. Then, when you find what you are looking for, click on the facility for more information!
View Facility Events
If a facility has a public calendar, you can view it at the bottom of the facility’s page. The calendar will show any events that are taking place at the facility and you can click on the event for more information. If the facility contains any subfacilities, you will be able to select which ones you want to see directly on the main facility’s calendar. Sign up for iCal Updates in order to add events to your own personal calendars automatically!
Share Information with Your Friends
Quickly and easily share facility information with your friends using Facebook, Twitter, Google Plus, or Email.
Account Owner Features
As a site account owner, there are several features made available just to you:
Rate Facilities : Contribute to the website and help others by rating the facilities that you have been to.
Reserve Facilities : Book a facility online for your special event. Just fill out the form, make your payment (if applicable), and you’re done! You can even book the facility for recurring events if you need to.
Save Your Searches : If you search using the same criteria on a regular basis, save the search so that you don’t have to fill out the information each time.
Submit a Missing Facility : Is something missing from our list? Let us know if we have missed anything by sending us the name and any important details so that we can add it to the website.
Subscribe to iCal : Want to stay up to date on what is happening at your favorite facility? Subscribe to iCal and the events will be added to your personal calendar automatically!

Welcome to Phipps Park Campground!
Phipps Park Campground, located at 2175 SW Locks Road in Stuart, Florida, spans the Okeechobee Waterway, encompassing 55 acres of conservation and camping space. It offers excellent year-round fishing opportunities in both fresh and saltwater. Enjoy scenic waterfront views from your campsite!

Campground Amenities
99 RV sites (with 20/30/50-amp electric service, water, sewer, picnic table and fire ring)
19 Adventure Tent sites (with a 10x10 canvas tent, grill, picnic table and fire pit). Seasonal availability (Nov 1–May 31)
Boat ramp and dock
Hot water showers
Fishing pier
Firewood (available for purchase)
Free WiFi

Check-In and Check-Out:
Check-in: Begins at 3 p.m. You can check in online using the guest portal or visit the office. During park hours, the gate is open. Campers manage the gate for visitors after 7:30 p.m.
Check-out: Before 11 a.m.
Reservation Changes:
Cancellations: Email phippspark@martin.fl.us at least 14 days before arrival for a refund. No refunds within 14 days.
Extensions: Make a new reservation online. For assistance, visit the office, call (772) 475-7433 , or email phippspark@martin.fl.us
Gate Access:
Hours: Gate opens at 6 a.m., closes at 7:30 p.m.
Code: Sent via email upon reservation and weekly for longer stays.
Pets:
You may bring up to 2 vaccinated pets to your campsite, which must be leashed and cleaned up after. Please note that dogs are not permitted in the adventure tent area.
Campsite Setup:
We do not allow personal tent camping; however, adventure tents are available for rent.
Utilities: Report issues to staff during office hours or email.
Campsite Etiquette:
Music: Allowed; quiet hours from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Fire Pits: Use firewood only; available for purchase at the office.
Parking:
2 vehicles or 1 vehicle + trailer per site in the gravel area. Additional parking at the gate and pavilion.
Boats:
You can bring a boat; park on your RV site or at the boat ramp.
Text (ID: 11678)
Explore Martin County
Martin County is Florida’s hidden gem, offering the perfect backdrop for relaxation and connection. With soft sand beaches ideal for sunbathing, swimming, and unforgettable snapshots, Martin County invites you to unwind.
Explore a variety of family activities during your visit, from rodeos to upscale shopping, art galleries, museums, and eco-friendly sea turtle adventures. It’s a place to escape and make memories that last longer than tan lines. Learn more at Discover Martin
Leave No Trace
Help us preserve Martin County’s natural beauty. Please follow the Leave No Trace 7 Principles during your stay at Phipps Park, ensuring future generations can enjoy this stunning park as much as you do!
Reservations
To make a reservation online, or to modify an existing reservation, please select from the buttons below. Reservations should be made at least 24 hours in advance of your arrival to ensure timely delivery of the gate code for after-hours park entry.
Make a Reservation
Modify Reservation
Refund policy
Cancellations, date transfers and refunds must be made fourteen (14) days prior to the reserved arrival date. No refunds or transfers will be granted for cancellations or transfers made less than 14 days from the arrival date. This means you lose your reservation payment.
A $25 cancellation fee will be applied to the refund request for campsites with reservation dates lasting between 1 and 14 nights.
A $100 cancellation fee will be applied to the refund request for campsites with reservation dates lasting between 15 and 29 days.
A $300 cancellation fee will be applied to the refund request for campsites with reservation dates that are 30 nights or greater.
Cancellation requests must be submitted in writing by contacting Phipps Park Campground via email at phippspark@martin.fl.us . All requests must be accompanied by the reservation email receipt, site number and name of the person who made the reservation.
In the event the Campground closes due to Tropical Storms, Hurricanes, or required maintenance, customers will receive a refund for the duration of the closure.
Rules and regulations
Reservations & Check-In / Out
Same Day Reservations: Must be made by 5 p.m.
Check-In/Out: Check-in time is 3:00 p.m. and check-out time is 11:00 a.m.
Payment: Must be made in advance. The park prohibits the use of campsites without payment. Camping equipment will be stored at the owner’s expense if camping fees are not paid within 24 hours after the allocated registration time.
Gate Access
Gate Hours: The front gate opens at 6 a.m. and closes at 7:30 p.m. Campers are provided a gate code for after-hours access. Campers must open and close the gate for visitors arriving after 7:30 p.m.
Camping Policies
Recreational Use Only: Adventure Tent camping and RV sites are restricted to recreational use.
Camping Permit: No person is authorized to camp or sleep in the park unless he/she has obtained a park permit.
Allowed Accommodations: Overnight sleeping in a RV, travel trailer, pop-up camper, fifth wheel, camper van and camper truck is permitted. Car camping, including camping in a truck, van or SUV, is prohibited. Phipps Park does not allow tent camping or converted trailers and school buses. Platform tents are available for rental.
Capacity: Campsites are designated to hold a maximum of six (6) people.
Full Service Site Requirement: All registered guests staying in a full-service Recreational Vehicle site must have on site either:
A fully operational self-propelled Recreational Vehicle or
A functional vehicle with sufficient towing capacity to remove their RV trailer from the premises when required or notified by park staff.
Duration Limits
RV Camping: Limited to 90 days within 300 consecutive days. Reservations exceeding this limit will be canceled and will not be eligible for a refund.
Adventure Tent Camping: Limited to 14 days within a 6-month period. No more than 4 nights consecutively. Reservations exceeding this limit will be canceled and will not be eligible for a refund.
Campsite Maintenance & Vehicle Policies
Campsite Condition: Must be maintained in a neat and orderly condition.
Vehicle Storage: Overnight storage of recreational vehicles, boats, trailers and other vehicles is not permitted except with an active camping permit and physical presence of the registered camper. Maximum of two vehicles per site; a trailer or motorcycle can replace the second car. Additional camping units and vehicles require an extra reservation and/or fee. Boat trailers must be placed on the south side of the boat ramp, locked and secured.
Proof of Registration: Campers must provide proof of registration for all vehicles and trailers upon request.
Prohibited Items & Activities
Use of Property: No screws or nails in trees or park property. Use of pallets or scrap lumber for firewood is not permitted.
Activities: No smoking within 50 feet of all buildings. No fireworks, golfing, or vehicle washing/repairing in the park.
Dishwashing and Laundry: Prohibited in bathrooms.
Transporting Waste: Transport black or gray water only in approved containers. Use the dump station for disposal.
Lines/Ropes: Not permitted to be tied to trees.
Quiet Hours & Facility Hours
Quiet Hours: From 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.
Laundry Room Hours: From 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
Pets
Limits and Restrictions: There is a limit of two pets per campsite. Pets must be kept on the campsite or be restrained with a leash six feet or less. Pet owners must be able to show proof of vaccinations and licenses upon request. Pet waste must be picked up by owners, consistent with Section 9.92.B., General Ordinances, Martin County Code. Section 9.90, General Ordinances, Martin County Code regarding animal restraints, is strictly enforced.
Adventure Tents Area: Pets are not allowed overnight.
General Rules
Conduct: Persons under 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Parents are responsible for their children’s conduct.
Overnight Absence: Inform the Park Supervisor if you are planning to be away from the campsite overnight.
Compliance: All persons must comply with Federal, State & Local laws. The person registering is responsible for seeing that all members of his or her party and guests obey park rules. Failure to observe and comply with park rules, county ordinances or laws may result in forfeiture of camping privileges.
Please take proper precautions to secure your property/equipment as Phipps Park will not be responsible for thefts or damage.
