RV Camping
Phipps Park Campground offers a variety of scenic sites to accommodate your RV needs. Choose from 58 waterfront and 41 interior sites, totaling 99 RV (recreational vehicle) spots, each equipped with 20/30/50-amp electric service, water and sewer hookups, a picnic table, and fire pit.
RV camping is limited to a maximum stay of 90 days within a consecutive 300-day period. Reservations exceeding this 90-day limit will be cancelled and are non-refundable.

The 2026 Camping Season will run from May 8th to October 11th.
Reservations cannot be made any earlier than 180 days from your stay date, January 1 st Reservations open for the new year.
RESERVATION SLIPS WILL NO LONGER BE PROVIDED. If you have a question regarding your reservation, you can call 218-546-5021, M-F, 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m. After hours, there will be a reservation list posted in the City Hall entrance window facing 2nd Street SW for verification.
The 2026 Camping Season will run from May 8th to October 11th.
Reservations cannot be made any earlier than 180 days from your stay date.
Quiet time is from 10:00 p.m. - 8:00 a.m.
(Please respect other guests by lowering your voices and turning off any music during this timeframe.) PROFANITY WILL NOT BE TOLERATED.
Pets MUST BE cleaned up after and leashed at all times.
There is no lifeguard on duty at our beach.
None of our campsites are pull-through.
Camping units MUST FIT bumper to bumper into each site.
Camping check-ins are after 2:00 p.m. on date of arrival
Camping check-outs are at 12:00 Noon on date of departure.
Advanced Pre-paid Reservations are recommended.
THERE ARE NO REFUNDS FOR CANCELLATIONS.
There is a 2-night camping minimum on both Memorial Day and Labor Day Holiday weekends.
There is a 2-night camping minimum on all weekends.
We do NOT provide RV dump services.
Crosby Memorial Park Campground does not provide WIFI.
The Cook Shack and Bandshell can be rented daily from 8:00 a.m .- 10:00 p.m.
Cook Shack and Bandshell keys can be picked up at City Hall Monday - Friday between 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m. prior to your rental.
If you have any technical difficulties during your stay, please contact the Crosby Public Works Department at 218-839-3449.
In the event of an emergency, please call 911. The nearest hospital is Cuyuna Regional Medical Center within the Crosby city limits.

Search Facebook Instagram Twitter Hatbox Event Park 2025 Events 2024 Events 2023 Events RV Park Home Park Facilities & Rentals Hatbox Event Park RV Park Hatbox RV Park Hatbox RV Campsite was developed to support special events happening in the Muskogee area. The campsite is located on the east runway. It is an asphalt surface, with over 150 defined RV slips with full hook-up electric, water, and sewer. RV campsites are located adjacent to the Love-Hatbox Sports Complex baseball, softball, soccer, and football fields. The complex is also home to the River Country Family Water Park open Memorial Weekend-Labor Day. Centennial Trail is a paved 3.2 mile walking and bicycling trail circling the complex; traveling east on the trail leads (2.0 miles) to downtown Muskogee. Book your stay - ONLINE RV RESERVATION SYSTEM Cost per RV site*: $30 Per Night Fee $175 Weekly Rate (7 consecutive days) *Reservation availability and fees subject to change for special events. See "Events and Festivals" webpage for more information. RV Site Address: 630 S. 40th Street, Muskogee, OK 74401. General Info and Rules HATBOX RV Campsite CLOSED November 15-March 10. Renters must be 18 years or older with a valid state-issued photo ID. Each RV site includes full hook-up - water, electricity (50 amp), sewer, and wifi. Water at slips winterized November-March. No shower or laundry facilities are available. Trash dumpsters are located on-site. The entry/exit gate is located on the east side of the hangar on South 40th Street. Speed Limit 10 mph. No parking in the grass. Clear campsite of all litter and debris. Trash must be bagged and deposited into refuse containers provided. Use of gas grills permitted; campfires and open fires are not permitted. Fireworks are prohibited. Pets on leash and accompanied by owner at all times. Animal droppings should be cleaned up immediately. No aggressive dogs or barking nuisance will be allowed. Parking is strictly at your own risk. The city of Muskogee is not responsible for your vehicle, its contents, or for personal injury or property damage sustained by you or your guests. The use of loud, foul, or vulgar language and threatening or reckless behavior is not permitted. Police will be notified and grounds for immediate eviction. Damage or destruction of property will be paid for by the responsible party. Respect the privacy of neighbors and no trespassing. Quiet time is 10:00pm-8:00am. Parents are responsible for the conduct and safety of their children. Accidents should be reported immediately to the Hatbox Office, 918-684-6305. For medical emergencies or immediate safety concerns, call 911. Management reserves the right to evict or refuse service to any person or persons who break or disregard any rules without refund. 918-684-6302 8:00am - 5:00pm information@ muskogeeparks.org 837 E Okmulgee Muskogee, OK 74403 © The City of Muskogee Parks & Recreation. Structures
No structures (including but not limited to patios, showers, decks etc.) may be built upon or moved on to the Camper’s space.
You cannot dig holes into the ground or screw bolts into the cement. These are considered structures and are not permitted.
Clotheslines
Not permitted
Alcohol
Not allowed in playground area; please drink responsibly
NO GLASS BOTTLES
Arms and firearms
NOT ALLOWED
Campfires
Campfires are NOT permitted to avoid ground wildfires.
Collecting
Take only memories and photographs. Federal and state laws prohibit collecting plants and animals and artifacts.
Firewood
Downed dead wood offers food and shelter to wildlife and provides essential nutrients for the soil. Please do not gather firewood.
Hammocks
NOT ALLOWED
Litter
Please deposit trash in dumpsters. Leaving no trace of your visit helps the park remain beautiful and reduces the possibility of human/animal conflicts.
Parking
Park only in designated areas to protect the plants and soil. Any vehicle encroaching on any other space shall be moved by Camper or it will be towed at camper’s expense.
VEHICLES
1 VEHICLE PER RV SITE / ADDITIONAL VEHICLES NEED TO BE PARKED AT PARKING LOT
Guests
Visiting guests are required to pay the entrance fee for daily user pass. No overnight privileges allowed.
Pets
Protect pets and wildlife by keeping pets on leashes, no longer than 6 feet, at all times.
Please pick up after your pets.
Quiet hours
Quiet hours are 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Respect your neighbors and celebrate nature's night noises.
Safe driving
Protect all park users and wildlife by obeying speed limits.
No passengers under 18 are permitted in truck beds.
Speed limit within the park is 10 mph.
NO DRIVING ON WALKING TRAIL
Swimming
Swimming in the Arroyo is NOT Permitted
Wildlife
Keep wildlife wild. Do not feed or harass wildlife.

Wonderful getaway with beautiful scenery
HIDDEN PINES RV PARK WELCOMES YOU
Pet-Friendly, Family-Friendly, and Affordable
Perfect for fisher folks, vacationers, retirees, nature-lovers, and workers
Newly remodeled Hidden Pines RV Park in Ore City has 5 star ratings from everyone! Get away from it all on the most beautiful lake in East Texas – Lake O’ the Pines. Tucked away in dense pine forest, your RV campsite directly overlooks the serene waters of the lake. Great fishing, gentle breezes, glorious sunsets, and quality time with your family, friends, and pets.
Sites and Rates
Vacation Amenities in a Pine Paradise
All the comforts of home…and then some!
We have a playground, fast reliable WiFi, fenced dog park, mile-long nature trail that goes around the lake, nearby boat launch, big RV sites shaded by large mature trees, lawn games, party pavilion, boat storage, friendly folks in the office, congenial campers, and lots more. Check it out – you’ll be amazed!
View all Amenities
Hidden Pines is a Hidden Gem
Fantastic location, best part of the lake to fish
Open all year, Hidden Pines RV Park offers the splendors of the changing seasons coupled with outdoor recreation. Spend lazy summer days fishing on the lake, go leaf-peeping in autumn at Barnwell Mountain Jeep & ATV Park, do winter holiday shopping at the antique stores in historic Jefferson, and hike the nature trails in spring – it’s an all-natural outdoor Paradise.
About
“An amazing hidden gem on Lake O’ The Pines! This was our 1st travel trailer camping experience and I am SO thankful we started off here. The playground is so nice! Views are amazing! The hiking trail was not too hard but just right. We even spotted some tracks on our hike (great teaching experience). Great place for families! They even stepped in and saved us a few times! All in all this is an awesome place and I can’t wait to come back. The summer months are going to be epic! If you’re looking for a place to camp, do yourself a favor and book now.”
Chelsey Y
Google Reviews
“I’m so excited for this park. Lake O’ The Pines has needed a premier RV park for quite some time and this is it! From the over-sized treed spots, a mile + long nature/ walking trail, a dog park, laundry facilities, and a brand new clean bathhouse, this park has it all. Not to mention the brand new highly secured enclosed boat storage and self-storage!”
Travis H
Google Reviews
“Incredible views of the lake! Updates galore to the park. New ownership and management have made some amazing upgrades. Great place to take your family for the weekend out on the lake for fishing and fun.”
Sam J
Google Reviews

Riverside Park Campground
Located within Riverside Park, along the banks of the Nechako River, the Riverside Park Campground is the perfect combination of camping in the woods and exploring small-town wonder. While far enough away to have an authentic camping experience, the Campground is only a 10-minute walk from downtown Vanderhoof for last-minute marshmallows or to take in some local cuisine.
The Riverside Park Campground has 38 camping sites, with two pull-through campsites and three spots with double sites. Each site allows for trailers and tents, and all have water and electricity connections available (five sites with 50A electrical service). There are bathrooms and showers available for all campers within the park. Click here to view the campground map.
The park gates are open from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM. Free Wi-Fi is available at the campground office. Access to the park amenities is just a few steps away: playground, walking and running path, covered picnic area, beach volleyball court, unsupervised waterfront, and more!
The Riverside Park Campground operates seasonally. In 2026, the park will be open May 6 through October 4. Reservations may be made beginning January 1, 2026.
The campground is closed to bookings from July 2-6, 2026 due to the Centennial Event being held in Riverside Park.
Book a Campsite
If you already have a reservation, click here to visit our guest portal.
For questions or assistance, email booking@vanderhoof.ca .
Campground Policies
Provincial Parks
Provincial Parks are maintained by the Province of BC. They usually offer services and can be reserved online.
BC Parks
Recreation Sites
Vanderhoof is surrounded by a multitude of recreational campsites. These sites are developed and maintained by the Province of BC and are found by accessing BC’s network of Forest Service Roads. They are free, unserviced, non-reservable campsites which are generally more rustic than Provincial Parks. A Backroads Mapbook is a must-have for road-trippers in BC, which maps out all the recreation sites and trails in the Province. You can purchase a Backroads Mapbook at the Vanderhoof Tourism & Cultural Centre.
Sites and Trails BC
Resorts & Lodges
There are a number of resorts south of Vanderhoof, from 30 km to over 100 km out of town on gravel roads. Each resort offers its own unique experience from world-class fly-fishing to amazing Swiss cuisine. There are resorts which offer float plane charters, boat rentals, full-service cabin rentals, and rustic campsites. Whether you are interested in hunting and fishing or just a backwoods getaway there is a resort here just for you! With superb angling, excellent hunting, amazing hiking and photography including wildlife viewing at your fingertips, why wait?
Passing Through Town? A Day in Vanderhoof
Whether you are looking for an adventuresome way to stretch your legs, are an avid wildlife admirer eager to capture your next signature photo or looking for fun ways to entertain the family, Vanderhoof has something for you. Make the most of your day in Vanderhoof with the help of these sample itineraries.

Curbside Solid Waste Collection
To sign-up, call the District office at 250-567-4711 . On collection day, bins must be placed no further than 1 metre from the roadside and must be on the street by 8:00am.
Residents are responsible for the replacement cost if the bin is lost or stolen, and for keeping their bins clean and secure, and returning their bins to their property after collection. All bins have an electronic ID tag that is linked to your specific property, and must stay at the assigned residence even if you move.
If damage or vandalism of the bins results from negligence, residents will be responsible for obtaining a new bin from the District and paying the replacement cost. Please call 250-567-4711 to report your issue.

Weed Control
The District’s goal is to control weeds and grasses which may impair traffic visibility, damage road asphalt surfaces, that may cause safety issues for pedestrians and for aesthetic purposes.
The District controls weeds with mechanical trimming which includes roadside tractor mowing and weed line trimming. Another objective of the program is to minimize the collection of litter and debris in weed infested areas. The District takes a leadership role in keeping our municipality clean. Another objective is to support the BC Weed Control Act to manage noxious weeds. The District maintains road shoulders in all areas of the District of Vanderhoof. The road shoulders are mowed with a tractor equipped with a flail mower. Weed whacking is included in the program to maintain walkways, municipal facilities and other right of ways. The District of Vanderhoof requires all property owners and residents to maintain the boulevard(s) and lane adjacent to their property. The District does not provide this service and does not include any funds in the budget for such work. Most of this work involves landscape cutting, trimming and watering of grass on the boulevards and lanes. Property owners and residents are encouraged and expected to maintain the boulevards for the beautification of our district and the enjoyment of all.
If you have any concerns, please contact the Director of Public Works and Engineering at 778-916-0397 .

Sharps and other items related to drug consumption have become more common within Vanderhoof recently, and Public Works will remove these items from public spaces when reported.

Riverside Park Campground Policies
• Reservation holders must be at least 19 years of age and are responsible for the actions
of all party members.
• Maximum reservation length is 14 nights; 4 adults are permitted per campsite (add $5
each for up to 4 additional adults). Children stay free of charge, up to a maximum site
occupancy of 8 people.
• Full payment is required to secure a reservation (sites cannot be held by a deposit).
• A non-refundable processing fee of $5 is collected by our booking platform once per site
reserved.
• Processing fees and optional lock fees are non-refundable. Site charges will be fully
refunded when cancelled with 7+ days notice, or 50% refunded for 1-6 days notice.
• Cash reservations are non-refundable.
• Same-day cancellations or no-shows are not eligible for refunds.
• Refunds for a multi-day reservation will be calculated by the amount of notice provided
for each date cancelled.
• All parties agree that the occupier may be evicted without a reason, or may vacate
without notice, however, refunds are not given for an eviction or vacating your campsite
early without notice.
• Sites reserved for more than one night are held until 11 AM the day after the scheduled
arrival date. If we have not heard from you by this time, the remaining days of your
reservation will be cancelled. All fees paid will be forfeited.
• Use the park and facilities at your own risk.
• Check in between 12:00 noon and 9:00 PM on arrival; check out by 11:00 AM on the date
of departure.
• Put away all food and coolers when not in use to prevent wildlife encounters; do not
clean fish at campsites.
• Alcohol may only be consumed on a reserved campsite.
• Campfire use is subject to restrictions. Please refer
to https://wildfiresituation.nrs.gov.bc.ca/map
• Campfires must be in designated fire pits; do not leave fires unattended.
• Only use firewood provided if available; do not gather or cut vegetation or trees from
around your site.
• Parking is not permitted on the roadway.
• Campground quiet hours are from 10pm to 7am; no music or generators are permitted
during this time.
• Campground speed limit is 10 km/h.
• Pets must be leashed.
• WIFI is available at the campground office (does not reach campsites).

KOLOB CAMPGROUND WELCOMES YOU
Camping near Zion National Park, Kolob Reservoir, Subway Canyon Zion, and Zion West Rim Trail. Near Virgin Utah, Cedar Breaks, and St. George, Utah.
Since opening our doors in 1967, Kolob Campground has welcomed thousands of guests. Situated near Kolob Reservoir, Zion National Park, and The West Rim Trail to Angels Landing. This privative dry camp is the perfect location to start your Zion National Park adventure. Greater Zion
Contact
Home: Welcome
ABOUT US
Hosting Campers since 1967. The perfect way to escape the heat of summer, and the crowds of Zion National Park. Kolob Campground, Kolob Terrace Road, and Kolob Reservoir is a quiet location nestled between the main canyons of Zion National Park and the remote Kolob Finger Canyons Complex at Zion National Park. With quick access to West Rim Trail, Subway Canyon, Hop Valley Trail, and Wildcat Canyon Trail, this area of Greater Zion is not to be missed.
Home: About
Home: Blog Feed
AMENITIES & SERVICES
Camping is one of life's great pleasures. Finding a great campsite can be a challenge. At Kolob Campground, we have partnered with hipcamp to ensure you have the ability to reserve the campsite perfect for you. Check out our site and let us know if there’s anything else we can do for you.
VEHICLE ACCESS
Kolob Campground provides you with the campsites you need for an enjoyable outdoor experience. Large RV/Trailer parking limited to sites 1,2,4,9,16,18,19,20 If these are not available contact the camp host for other possible accommodations. Some pull through locations are available. Contact camp host for details on RV sites prior to booking. Tent camping is appropriate at all campsites.
FIRE PITS
Fire Pits are always available at each campsite. Due to dry conditions, and risk of wildfires, a fire ban has been enacted for Kolob Mountain. The use of Gas Firepits, Gas Stoves, and Gas BBQ's are still allowed. As a reminder, Kolob Campground offers Firepits to campers for a nominal fee of $50 for your entire stay. This includes one large tank of propane.

Welcome to the Okanogan County Fairgrounds RV Campground!
Please note before booking:
Refund Policy:
No refunds are issued. Reservation credit for future use will be added to your account if cancellation occurs.
**We are a multi-use community fairgrounds facility , rented events may be taking place on the Fairgrounds during your stay.
While we strive to maintain a comfortable campground experience, there may be increased traffic or activity at times.
By completing your reservation, you confirm that you have read and agree to our campground rules and policies.

RV PARK RULES
14 DAY STAY MAXIMUM
1. Quiet Hours: 10:00pm – 6:30am.
> Due to events, Saturday quiet hours begin at 1:00am.
2. No visitors after 10pm.
3. Pets must be leashed. Please clean up messes.
4. Please DO NOT park vehicle in an empty space.
5. Do not set up tent in hook-up space.
6. NO CAMPFIRES!
7. Check out time is 12pm noon.
PAYMENT: RESTROOMS/SHOWERS:

rooms/bath houses. Anyone dumping sewage in restrooms is subject

ELECTRIC: garbage. No appliances.
If you are not present at your RV, please do not run your AC.
BOATS:
Additional fee of $100 will be billed if we witness this occurring.
Boat trailers must be kept in designated trailer storage area.
QUIET TIME: Management must approve of any boats to be kept on site and
10PM to 6:30AM, Noise should not be heard from your campsite camper may be requested to leave boat in designated area.

management reserves the right to ask camper to do so.

under control. No more than 2 pets.

immediately. No refunds in these circumstances.
MAINTENANCE/EMERGENCY:
VISITORS: Report any maintenance problem, emergency to the facility
No visitors after 10pm please. immediately. Please call us with any emergencies 509-740-
9009 when appropriate.
TENTS:
Only 1 tent (for sleeping) allowed per site.

in use to keep grass alive. No large canopy tents without permission No washing of cars or boats. Leaky hoses and water connections
granted from office. must be addressed immediately.
NOT PERMITTED:
Firearms, BB or pellet guns, fireworks, speeding over 5 miles per hour, littering, permanent clothes lines illegal drugs, underage drinking,
loud parties, reckless behavior, disorderly conduct, intoxication, rock throwing, sling shots, alcohol off campsite. No smoking in bathrooms.
Please take proper measures to protect your property. The licensee accepts camping privileges with the understanding that he/or she does hereby release the

LA PAZ COUNTY
PUBLIC NOTICE
DON T PAVILION ADA IMPROVEMENTS
LA PAZ COUNTY PARK
7350 RIVERSIDE DRIVE, PARKER AZ
The County of La Paz has been awarded a federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) from the State of Arizona Department of Housing (ADOH) and will accept bids from qualified firms or individuals with a minimum of a B-2 commercial license as registered with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors, and registered with SAM.gov to perform the following services: Rehabilitation of current restrooms to comply with current ADA requirements including; new stalls, handicapped toilets, grab bars, handicapped sinks, paper dispensers, and entry doors. If funding allows project to include the replacement of two air conditioning units and patching of the roof.
To obtain bid package as well as additional bidding procedures contact: Grant Consultant, Denise Bishop, Dbishop Consulting, phone number: (928) 208-5841: or e-mail: dbishopconsulting04@hotmail.com. Kimball Dam Water Reservoir
Kimball Dam Water Reservoir
The City of Calistoga owns and operates a water reservoir and a conventional surface water treatment facility four miles northwest of the city. This water resource produces approximately one third of the total annual water demand for the community.
The City’s water reservoir was originally named Ghisolfo Reservoir. It has since been known and referred to commonly as Kimball Reservoir. This reservoir has a surface drainage area of approximately 3.4 square miles. The City owns a portion of the surrounding watershed with the remainder owned by the Napa County Land Trust, State Parks Department, and a private landowner.
Kimball Canyon Dam was constructed in 1939 by the City and was subsequently raised in 1948 to increase the storage capacity of the reservoir. The dam is an earthfill structure approximately 300 feet long, 200 feet wide at the base, and about 75 feet high. The spillway crest elevation is 575 feet above mean sea level.
The original storage capacity of the reservoir measured in a 1954 survey; at the spillway crest was approximately 345 acre-feet and 409 acre feet at the top of the flashboards (elevation 579 feet). The accumulation of sediment in the reservoir has since reduced the storage capacity.
In 2013, the City preformed a capacity survey that included bathymetry and determined storage of 267 acre-feet at the top of the spillway and 328 acre-feet at the top of the flashboards. There has been a loss of approximately 78 acre-feet between the 1954 and 2013 survey which extrapolates to an approximate annual sediment loss of 1.3 acre-feet annually.
Reservoir capacity loss is driven by sediment from stormwater runoff, with wildfires in 1964, 1985, 2017 and 2021 markedly increasing sediment displacement, particularly in the first winter after the fires.
Annual inspections of the reservoir are conducted by the State Division of Dam Safety. These routine visual inspections are conducted by the state to ensure the structure is satisfactory for continued use.

Onsite Camping For Event Attendees & Participants
RV Park
Stay in comfort when you attend an @the Grounds event or travel in the Placer County.
Affordable Rates & Comfortable Amenities
@the Grounds RV Park offers convenient access to any event held on the @the Grounds campus, as well as the excitement of the surrounding Placer County .
Full hookups are available at every site
$50 per night per space
Space is limited.
Check for availability online, in the portal below.
Reservations may be made up to 6 months in advance.
We offer a maximum stay of 28 days, followed by a required 10-day cooling-off period before returning.
We do not offer shower facilities or laundry facilities.
Office hours: Monday - Friday 9 am-5 pm
After-hours by appointment only
RV Park is partially closed during the month of June for the annual Placer County Fair.

@THE GROUNDS RV PARK RULES AND POLICIES
RV Park Requirements
• All RV’s entering the grounds are subject to inspection and must be cleared by management to
stay within the RV Park.
• Generally, RVs older than 15 years are not allowed; some exceptions may apply.
• The RV must be in good, clean, and operable condition. RVs in obvious disrepair will not be
allowed to stay.
• All RVs must be self-contained. There are no showers, restrooms, or laundry facilities available.
• Boats, extra trailers, jet skis, or other recreational vehicles are not allowed and cannot stay in the
RV park.
• Trailer tow vehicles must be present with the RV throughout stay. No towing in, or RV being
dropped off by an outside party.
General Occupancy Rules
• Quiet hours are from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. daily. Absolutely no unnecessary, loud, or disruptive noise
of any kind is allowed. Please ensure that speakers, radios, televisions, or other machinery do
not emit sound beyond your assigned space. Vehicles with abnormally loud exhaust systems are
not allowed inside the facility.
• All signs posted notices and directions of the RV hosts and/or management must be obeyed.
Non-compliance may result in immediate removal without a refund.
• No selling, advertising, conducting business, or distribution of any product (including alcohol).
• No loitering in the RV or grounds area, all occupants must be registered with the RV Park and/or
have official business with the @the Grounds.
• No hazardous or illegal materials may be brought on the premises.
• Illegal drugs, firearms, and/or any other type of weapon are prohibited on the @the Grounds
campus.
• RV occupants must wear a shirt, pants/shorts, and footwear when outside their RV.
• Occupants and guests must follow all applicable laws and regulations.
• No recreational use of skateboards, motorbikes, scooters, or roller skates is allowed.
• SMOKING IS NOT ALLOWED in or within 25 feet of buildings. Please use proper receptacles
when extinguishing cigarettes. DO NOT discard cigarette butts on the ground.
• Any illegal activity, disorderly or disturbing conduct, drunkenness, profanity, rowdy behavior,
fighting or illegal drug use of any kind is grounds for immediate removal from the facility. No
refunds will be given for occupants or guests that are removed.
Pets
• Dogs and other pets must be placed in a pen/cage when left out of the RV and must be on a
leash when walked by the applicant.
• All animal droppings must be cleaned up and disposed of in the trash receptacles.
• Pets must not be a nuisance or threat to other park users. Excessive barking is not allowed. Any
threat or continued nuisance will result in the immediate removal of the RV occupant with no
refund.
• Pets are not allowed in buildings, except for service dogs and during dog shows.
• Management has the right to reject any pet.
Guests and Children
• Children 17 and younger must always be under parental or adult supervision.
• Children must be supervised, and parents/guardians must assume responsibility for all actions
of their children and guests.
• Please respect the privacy of fellow campers – do not walk through sites.
• All additional vehicles and visitors must park on the other side of the rod-iron fence. No visitors
after 10:00pm.
Grounds and Facilities
• The speed limit is 5 MPH – NO EXCEPTIONS. Failure to abide by the speed limit will be
considered grounds for immediate eviction. All vehicles that are not operational will be
considered abandoned and will be removed.
• No gray water, sewage, or effluent from sinks, toilets, and any other plumbing fixtures are to be
drained, dumped, or leak directly upon or into ground surfaces.
• All RVs and vehicles must park in the assigned location. Parking in vacant RV spaces and fire
lanes is prohibited and may result in the vehicle being towed at the owner’s expense.
• Washing of RVs or working on vehicle(s) is prohibited in the RV park or any of the @the Grounds
parking lots.
• No storage is permitted under or around RVs. Electrical appliances, storage boxes or
combustible material may not be stored or used outside or stored under or around RVs.
Clotheslines and wind brakes are not permitted.
• All trash is to be disposed of in the receptacles provided.
• Do not hang articles of clothing on fencing or trees.
• Fireworks and fires are not permitted, including pits, rings, etc. Self-contained, small propane
BBQ’s are allowed.
• Occupants and guests shall return the RV space and surrounding area in the same condition
that existed at the beginning of the stay.
@the Grounds Rental Events
• RV’s may be required to relocate on grounds with one day’s notice or be moved in case of an
emergency or rental event.
• Contracted events may have exceptions to certain rules of the RV park.
• The RV area is part of @the Grounds. At times there may be noise-generating events that take
place on the grounds. Please note that curfew times for events may exceed those of the RV
park.
• RV Park rental DOES NOT include admission to any @the Grounds events.
RV Park Policies
• Occupants shall be fully responsible for their use of the premises and any loss, damage, injuries,
and liability arising therefrom. Management shall not be responsible or liable for any theft, loss,
injury, or damage to any person(s) or property arising from such use.
• The park is made available in an “as is” condition for use by occupants and guests AT THEIR
SOLE RISK. To the maximum extent allowed by law, management shall have no disclosure or
security obligations and no duty to warn of any hazardous conditions.
• The right to occupy any space may not be transferred, assigned, or sublet.
• Occupants shall hold harmless, indemnify, and defend management and the County of Placer
from all damages, demands, expenses, losses, claims, and liabilities arising from or related to
occupant’s use of the premises and/or any breach of this agreement, including reasonable
attorney’s fees and all costs of defense.
• Management reserves the right to refuse entry and occupancy for any lawful reason.
Management reserves the right to make changes to the rules, policies, and fees after written
notice thereof. Except as otherwise provided by law, occupants and their vehicles may be removed
from the premises without a judicial hearing upon 72 hours written notice for a failure to pay the
full amount of space rental fee when due or for any failure to comply with these written rules and
policies.

Welcome to Starlight Campground & RV Park
Reservations can be made 365 days in advance of your arrival date by calling 231-535-0461 or by booking online .
Starlight Campground is a family friendly campground in northern Michigan nestled amidst mature pine trees, with cozy campsites, full facilities, a beautiful hiking trail, both vintage and contemporary trailer rentals, impeccably clean facilities, incredible sunsets, and star-filled night skies. It is those dark skies that have inspired our name, carried over into our Starry Nights Weekend during the annual Perseids meteor shower in August, just one of a season full of themed weekends filled with carefully planned activities.
Here at Starlight Campground we strive to provide our guests with a level of hospitality and service that will exceed their expectations. We are home of the “Welcome Wood”, where you will find three pieces of firewood already in your campfire ring as our way of saying “Thank you” for being our guest. We will even deliver wood, ice, and store items directly to your site. Think of it as room service in the great outdoors!
Northern Michigan has been attracting summer residents and visitors for over a century,
a tradition that continues to draw folks to its intriguing small towns, incredible beaches
on Lake Michigan, parks, festivals, and what is some of the greatest of the great
outdoors. Starlight Campground, located near Lake Bellaire and within 30 minutes of Torch Lake and midway between
Traverse City and Petoskey, brings access to all of that wonderment to today’s
generation of family campers, whether staying in anything from tents to big rig RV’s and
motorhomes. Please accept our invitation to be our guests at Starlight Campground for
your next family camping adventure!
Your hosts, Jeff and Samantha Byrne

Camping Policies
Check-in time is from 2:00 PM - 10:00 PM. Checking in after 10:00 PM is discouraged out of courtesy to fellow campers.
Check-out time is 12:00 Noon. Please be sure to check out by noon so
that we can ready the site for the next camper; late check-out may be able
to be arranged, based on availability, for a small additional fee if staying
past 2:00 PM.
RV sites are intended for a single family and a single camping unit (motor home, toy hauler, travel trailer, 5th wheel, truck camper, van camper,
or pop-up trailer). A small pup style (2 person) tent for children or a dining tent may also be used on your site.
Tents (with the exception of small 2 person pup tents for children that accompany RV's) are not allowed on RV sites without prior approval from management. Anyone booking an RV site with the intention of camping in a tent will be asked to move to a tent site if prior approval has not been obtained. If no tent sites are available you may be asked to leave without refund. Tent camping will not be approved by management on any of the Hilltop sites unless it is a small 2 person pup-tent for children, accompanied by an RV.
For tent-only campsites, as many tents as necessary to accommodate a single camping party are permitted within the boundaries of the site.
Rates are based on 2 adults and their dependent children under the age of 18. Additional adults can stay with you on your site for $7 per adult, per day. Children over 18 are considered adults.
Per the State of Michigan no more than 8 people (adults/children) are allowed on a campsite. We are happy to make arrangements for you to reserve another site if you have more than 8 people staying with you.
You must be 21 years old or older to reserve a campsite.
We allow for 2 vehicles per site, as long as both vehicles fit ON your site. Your vehicle total per site includes any boats, ATV/OHRVs, golf carts. Extra vehicles must be parked in our guest parking area near the Registration Building. If you would like your OHRV, boat or golf cart parked on your site then you must park any extra vehicles in guest parking.
All vehicles MUST be registered and MUST have a hang tag displayed on the rearview mirror. This includes guest vehicles.
EV charging is not allowed without prior approval. EV charging is $15/4 hours once approval is obtained.
The speed limit in the campground is 5 mph. This is to protect our little campers and to provide an enjoyable camping experience for all. Please go SLOW through the campground!
Quiet hours are from 10:00 PM - 8:00 AM. This doesn’t mean you have to go to bed at 10:00
PM, but all music should be turned off and voices around the campfire should be kept low. Please be courteous to your fellow campers who may have little ones trying to sleep and for those who go to bed early.
A deposit of one night’s camping fee is required to reserve a camp site.
There is a 2-night minimum stay for holiday weekends. Our holiday weekends are Memorial Day, 4th of July and Labor Day.
Campsite Cancellations - 48 hours cancellation notice is required. Notify us by phone by noon EST, more than two days before your scheduled arrival to receive your deposit refund, minus a $10 cancellation fee. Cancellations within 48 hrs will forfeit one night. All Holidays have a 1 night non-refundable deposit however full credit for future dates can be used with 2 week cancellation notice. Holidays include: Memorial Day, 4th of July, and Labor Day. Cancellations may only be done by phone, we are unable to accept cancellations via email or text.
REFUNDS: Please remember that camping is an outdoor activity. No refunds will be given for weather or for other discomforts of nature, or for early departures.
Specific sites are not guaranteed unless you elect to pay the Lock Site Fee. Although we try to honor all requests for sites there are times when we may need to move your reservation to another site of equal or better category. We do this only when absolutely necessary.
Lock Site - "Lock Site" is a new feature that allows a guest to reserve a specific site(s). During the reservation process, an option is offered to lock the site that you have chosen. This feature offers guests the opportunity to guarantee a specific site of their choice for a one time, non-refundable fee of $10. The one-time fee is assessed per reservation. While the Lock Site fee is a non-refundable fee, if a guest chooses to use it for their reservation, the deposit will follow normal cancellation policies which can be viewed under "Camping Policies".
Early check in before noon is $15, Late check out until 6pm is $15. All Late check outs need to be arranged in advance at the office, late check outs without advance notice will be automatically charged $15.
No Shows/Early Check-Out - All reservations will be held until 9:00 AM the morning following your scheduled arrival. If you have not arrived, called to cancel your reservation or informed us of a next day arrival by phone, your reservation will be considered a no-show and canceled without a refund. Cancellations may only be done by phone, we are unable to accept cancellations via email or text. No refunds for early check out on Holiday or special event weekends. No refunds for early check outs on RV rental units at any time.
There is a $4.00 processing fee for reservations.
Prohibited: Firearms, fireworks (including sparklers and pop-its), portable generators, chainsaws, Chinese lanterns, and drones.
Photographing and Filming - While a guest at the campground, you may appear in pictures or film that may be used in advertising, news reporting, public relations or other activities regarding the campground. Reservations at the campground or a visitor's day use pass constitute your consent for Starlight Campground and RV Park to use any pictures or films it deems appropriate without payment, inspection or review.
This park is a privately held property and as such, we reserve the right to remove anyone whose conduct or language is disruptive to others, or if they break any of the rules we have in place for the campground, without a refund.
Rentals
Check-in: 3:00 PM
Check-out: 11:00 AM
No smoking and no pets allowed in rentals
Cancellations - 7 days cancellation notice required. Please notify us by phone more than one week before your scheduled arrival to receive your deposit refund, minus a $10 cancellation fee. Cancellations 7 days or less from arrival date will forfeit 50% of deposit. Cancellations within 48 hrs of arrival date forfeit full deposit amount. All Holidays have a 1 night non-refundable deposit however full credit for future dates can be used with 2 week cancellation notice. Holidays include: Memorial Day, 4th of July, and Labor Day. Cancellations may only be done by phone, we are unable to accept cancellations via email or text.
Campsites
Please do not walk through other peoples campsites.
No washing of vehicles or RVs on your campsite.
Please do not destroy our trees by cutting or breaking branches.
Help us keep our grass alive by only using breathable mats at your campsite. We have these mats for sale in the Camp Store if you need one.
All RV's, tents, EZ up awnings, vehicles and personal items must be kept within the parameters of your site.
Please do not wash dirty dishes at the water spigots.
Trash pick-up is at 10:00 AM and 8:00 PM. Please place trash bags by your site post at the designated times for pick up. Please do not leave trash out between pick up times or overnight. We are home to many little critters who will happily tear through your trash and leave a mess.
Please do not move picnic tables from other sites. If you need an extra picnic table please let us know. We will be happy to get one for you if one is available.
Please do not hang clotheslines from any trees in the park.
Hammocks may be hung on your site only as long as the ropes are not breaking tree branches and the trees are strong enough to support the hammock without damaging the tree. Hammocks are not allowed to be hung in ANY general use areas of the park.
Please use appropriate RV rated extension cords or adapters if they are needed. We have these available at the Camp Store if needed.
Please use an appropriate sewer connection to eliminate the chance for backsplash and odors! We have these available at the Camp Store if needed.
Campfires
We love campfires but not bonfires! Please be sure your campfire is under control at all times.
Do not move your fire ring. If there is a problem with the location of your fire ring just let us know and we will see what we can do!
Please extinguish your fire before leaving your site or going to bed at night.
No torches with flames are allowed.
Do not burn any trash, bottles, metal, cans etc. in your fire ring.
No Outside Firewood - Please help us protect and preserve our beautiful trees by not bringing firewood in from outside sources. The firewood we sell is inspected to be free of insects and obvious tree diseases. Please buy your firewood from us. We offer free onsite wood delivery for your convenience which can be purchased in the Camp Store. And remember the State of Michigan's recommendation
… BUY IT, BURN IT, LEAVE IT … at your camping destination.
Pool Policies
The Pool is open from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend.
Children under 14 must have adult (18 or older) supervision inside the pool area at all times; no running, no diving, no rough play and no hard balls in the pool.
Pool hours are from 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM.
No glass containers or food allowed in the pool area.
Please do not bring alcoholic beverages to the pool area.
There is no life guard on duty.
Recreational Areas
No smoking in any of the public use areas.
Please help keep our campground clean by disposing of any trash in appropriate trash receptacles.
No glass containers in public use areas.
Little Campers
All children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult at the pool at all times.
Please accompany your children to the bathrooms and shower facilities.
After dark children under 16 must be on their campsite unless accompanied by an adult or participating in a sponsored activity.
Most importantly, HAVE FUN!
Pet Policies
All pets must be registered with the office.
All pets must be on a 6' leash at all times while off your site and on a tie out while at your site, except in the dog park where they can be off leash.
Dogs MUST not be left unattended in the dog park. Owners need to be within the dog park area with their dogs at all times.
Pets that cannot stay quiet when left unattended in your trailer should not be left alone. If you leave and your pet causes excessive noise or becomes a disturbance to other guests you will be asked to take them with you when leaving your site or to take them to a nearby Doggie Day Care.
Pets are not allowed in the registration building, recreational building, or pool area.
Should pets become noisy, they must be brought inside/quieted immediately.
Pet owners are responsible for cleaning up after their pets. This includes both on and off your site.
All dog breeds are allowed, however any dog that displays any kind of aggressive or nuisance behavior is grounds for you to be asked to leave the park without refund.
OHRV Policies
• All Off-road vehicles must be registered and have a Starlight OHRV tag displayed on them. There is no cost for this tag.
We enjoy being near a great set of trails here at Starlight Campground and hope you have fun exploring them. For the comfort and safety of everyone we ask that you obey the following guidelines. When riding in the campground please use common sense when it comes to safety with your off-highway recreational vehicle (OHRV). Please review all state laws and rules before setting out for a days riding. Make sure you have all the gear you need and know what is expected of you by the state to avoid getting a ticket and ruining your visit.
MAXIMUM SPEED LIMIT IN THE CAMPGROUND IS 5 MPH FOR ALL VEHICLES. PLEASE GO SLOW!
Upon check in to the campground all guests bringing ATVs/ORVs/Trail Bikes etc. must sign an acknowledgement of the rules set forth by the campground.
The trail out of the campground is near the tent area, between lot 27 and 28. Please follow all trail signs as you proceed to the trail-head.
Helmet and eye protection use is required by those 18 years or younger.
Children under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times while driving an ATV in the campground.
Visitors to our campground guests that arrive on ATVs are not allowed to ride into the campground. They must park in guest parking by the Registration building, check in at the office, pay the visitor fee, and walk into the campground.
Always travel on the gravel campground roads (no cutting through the woods or campsites)
Use extreme caution when exiting the campground - STOP, LOOK AND LISTEN.
No riding in the campground or connector trail after dark. ALL ATVS MUST BE BACK IN THE CAMPGROUND 1/2 AN HOUR AFTER SUNSET.
Machines may not be run during the campgrounds quiet hours of 10:00 PM - 8:00 AM.
You may only use your ATV for transportation to and from your campsite to the connector trail. ATVs may not be used in the campground for any other purpose, i.e. visit other campers, go to the restroom, camp store, pool.
ATV riders are expected to operate their machines as quietly as possible to maintain a relaxing campground environment.
If you need to work on your ATV/UTV or Trail Bike etc., please be courteous. DO NOT rev your engine. No disposal of fluids is allowed. You must take all fluid with you. No washing of ATVs, ORVs trail bikes etc. is allowed in the campground.
Golf Cart Policies
All golf carts must be registered and there is a $10 charge for weekend and weekly stays up to 14 days, $25 charge for guests staying 15 days or longer.
All golf cart drivers must possess a valid driver’s license.
Only one golf cart allowed per camp site.
Valid proof of insurance of the golf cart must be provided upon check-in and
the golf cart must be specifically listed as covered, on the policy.
Golf carts must visibly display a registration sticker on the front of the golf
cart at all times.
Golf cart drivers must observe the 5 MPH speed limit at all times and stay on
designated campground roads ONLY. No driving on the grass, walkways or
hiking trail.
Registered golf carts may be driven in the park from 8 AM until dark IF YOU
HAVE HEADLIGHTS/TAILLIGHTS. Golf carts without headlights and
taillights may NOT be driven after dusk.
The person registering the golf cart is responsible for ANY and ALL actions
of the golf cart while in our park, regardless of who you let drive it. No
speeding, swerving, or reckless driving of any kind will be tolerated.
Golf carts must maintain quiet operation. Gasoline powered golf carts must
have a muffler.
Campers must charge or recharge electric golf carts on the meter at their
campsite only.
Do not trespass onto neighboring properties. Golf carts registered with our
park must remain in our park for the duration of your stay.
Disregarding any of these policies can result in immediate dismissal of your
golf cart from the park.
Policy Regarding Political Signs
In order to maintain a welcoming atmosphere for all who camp with us,
Starlight Campground an RV Park has adopted a no political signs, political
flags, political symbols or political relics policy.
While we fully support your constitutional right to freedom of speech on
public property, those rights do not extend to our private property at
Starlight Campground and RV Park. Any political sign, flag, symbol or relic
that is not permanently affixed to your vehicle or RV is not allowed to be
posted or hung anywhere on site. Anyone doing so will be asked to remove
the aforementioned items.
We do however, encourage you to fly the American flag, family name flags,
holiday flags and your favorite sports team’s flags.
Starlight Campground management reserves the right to evict anyone, without refund, who does not follow these rules, is disruptive to the enjoyment of other campers, or poses a danger to others in the campground. Please be careful and have fun.
